1.question: What did God create in the beginning according to Genesis 1:1?
1.explanation: Genesis 1:1 declares: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.'

1.question: What did God command to appear on the first day of creation?
1.explanation: God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light, separating light from darkness on Day One.

1.question: On the second day, what was created to separate the waters above from the waters below?
1.explanation: God made the expanse on Day Two to separate the waters under the expanse from the waters above it, calling it 'sky'.

1.question: What two things appeared when the waters under the heavens gathered together on Day Three?
1.explanation: The waters gathered into one place and dry ground appeared; God called the dry ground 'land' and the gathered waters 'seas'.

1.question: What kind of vegetation did the earth produce on the third day?
options: Plants bearing seed and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds
1.correctAnswer: Plants bearing seed and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds
1.explanation: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees bearing fruit with seed in it according to their kinds.

1.question: What purpose was given for the lights placed in the expanse of the sky on the fourth day?
options: To separate day from night and serve as signs for seasons, days, and years
To test the faith of mankind
To consume the water of the deep
1.correctAnswer: To separate day from night and serve as signs for seasons, days, and years
1.explanation: God set lights in the expanse to separate day from night, govern the day and night, and serve as signs to mark seasons, days, and years.

1.question: Which living creatures were created on the fifth day?
options: Cattle and beasts of the field
Creatures that swarm in the waters and winged birds of the air
1.correctAnswer: Creatures that swarm in the waters and winged birds of the air
1.explanation: On Day Five, God created great sea creatures and every living thing that teems in the waters, as well as winged birds.

1.question: Before creating humanity on Day Six, what category of creatures did God make?
options: Livestock, creeping things, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds
1.correctAnswer: Livestock, creeping things, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds
1.explanation: God commanded the earth to produce living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals.

1.question: According to Genesis 1:26–27, in whose image and likeness was humanity created?
options: In the image of the angels
In the image and likeness of God
In the image of the stars
In the likeness of the beasts
1.correctAnswer: In the image and likeness of God
1.explanation: God said, 'Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness.' Male and female He created them in the image of God.

1.question: How did God describe everything He had made at the conclusion of Day Six?
1.explanation: Genesis 1:31 states: 'God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.'

2.question: What did God do on the seventh day after finishing creation?
options: He rested from all His work, blessed the seventh day, and made it holy
He sent rain over the earth
2.correctAnswer: He rested from all His work, blessed the seventh day, and made it holy
2.explanation: By the seventh day God completed His work, rested from all His labor, blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.

2.question: How was the ground watered before rain had fallen upon the earth?
options: A mist (or spring) came up from the earth and watered the whole surface
2.correctAnswer: A mist (or spring) came up from the earth and watered the whole surface
2.explanation: The Lord God had not yet caused it to rain, but a mist or stream came up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground.

2.question: From what did the Lord God form the first man, and how did he become a living soul?
options: From gold and silver, energized by lightning
From the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
From sea foam, infused by celestial light
From the bark of the Tree of Life
2.correctAnswer: From the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
2.explanation: The Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.

2.question: Where did the Lord God plant the garden for man, and in which direction?
options: In the desert to the west
On Mount Ararat to the north
2.explanation: Genesis 2:8 states that the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden, placing the man He had formed there.

2.question: Which two special trees are specifically named as growing in the midst of the Garden of Eden?
options: The Cedar of Lebanon and the Olive Tree
The Tree of Life and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
The Fig Tree and the Oak Tree
The Almond Tree and the Palm Tree
2.correctAnswer: The Tree of Life and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
2.explanation: In the middle of the garden were the Tree of Life and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.

2.question: How many headwaters did the river flowing out of Eden divide into, and what were their names?
options: Three: Red Sea, Dead Sea, Mediterranean
Four: Pishon, Gihon, Tigris (Hiddekel), and Euphrates
2.correctAnswer: Four: Pishon, Gihon, Tigris (Hiddekel), and Euphrates
2.explanation: A river flowed from Eden to water the garden, dividing from there into four heads: Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, and Euphrates.

2.question: What primary duty did God give Adam when placing him into the Garden of Eden?
options: To cultivate (dress) and keep (guard) the garden
To build a boat for trade
To hunt the animals for leather
2.correctAnswer: To cultivate (dress) and keep (guard) the garden
2.explanation: The Lord God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to tend and keep it.

2.question: What command and consequence did God give to Adam regarding the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil?
options: He could eat it on the Sabbath
He must not eat of it; for in the day he eats of it he would surely die
He could eat the leaves but not the fruit
2.correctAnswer: He must not eat of it; for in the day he eats of it he would surely die
2.explanation: God commanded: 'You must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will certainly die.'

2.question: What observation did the Lord God make before bringing the animals to Adam to be named?
options: 'It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him'
2.correctAnswer: 'It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him'
2.explanation: The Lord God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.'

2.question: How was the first woman created, and what was Adam's joyful response?
options: From clay by the riverbank; Adam called her sister
From one of Adam's ribs during a deep sleep; Adam declared: 'This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh'
From a sunbeam; Adam called her daughter
She descended from heaven on a chariot
2.correctAnswer: From one of Adam's ribs during a deep sleep; Adam declared: 'This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh'
2.explanation: God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, took one of his ribs, and made it into a woman. Adam exclaimed: 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman!'

3.question: How did the serpent initiate conversation with the woman in Genesis 3:1?
options: By asking: 'Did God really say, You must not eat from any tree in the garden?'
By offering her gold and jewels
By claiming to be an angel of light
3.correctAnswer: By asking: 'Did God really say, You must not eat from any tree in the garden?'
3.explanation: The serpent was more crafty than any wild animal and asked the woman: 'Did God really say, You must not eat from any tree in the garden?'

3.question: What lie did the serpent tell the woman regarding eating the forbidden fruit?
options: 'You will certainly not die... your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil'
'God does not care what you eat'
'The fruit will make you live forever instantly'
3.correctAnswer: 'You will certainly not die... your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil'
3.explanation: The serpent directly contradicted God's warning, saying: 'You will certainly not die. For God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.'

3.question: What three things did the woman perceive about the tree before eating its fruit in Genesis 3:6?
options: Good for food, pleasing to the eye, and desirable for gaining wisdom
Bitter to taste, heavy to carry, and strange to smell
Cold to touch, dark in color, and noisy in the wind
Covered in thorns, poisonous to touch, and rotten
3.correctAnswer: Good for food, pleasing to the eye, and desirable for gaining wisdom
3.explanation: She saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, so she took some and ate it, and gave some to her husband.

3.question: What immediate realization came to the man and woman after eating the fruit, and how did they react?
options: They realized they could fly and leapt into the air
They realized they were naked, sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves
They built an altar of thanksgiving
3.correctAnswer: They realized they were naked, sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves
3.explanation: The eyes of both were opened and they realized they were naked; so they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.

3.question: What did Adam and his wife do when they heard the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day?
options: They ran to welcome Him with singing
They hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden
They climbed to the top of the mountain
3.correctAnswer: They hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden
3.explanation: They heard the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the Lord God among the trees.

3.question: What question did the Lord God call out to the man in Genesis 3:9?
3.explanation: Genesis 3:9 states: 'But the Lord God called to the man, Where are you?'

3.question: Whom did Adam blame when God asked if he had eaten from the forbidden tree?
options: The woman God put with him ('The woman you put here with me—she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it')
3.correctAnswer: The woman God put with him ('The woman you put here with me—she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it')
3.explanation: The man said: 'The woman you put here with me—she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it.'

3.question: What prophetic judgment did God pronounce upon the serpent in Genesis 3:15 (the Protoevangelium)?
options: The serpent would gain wings and fly away
Enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between its offspring and hers; her offspring would crush its head, and it would strike his heel
The serpent would be honored as the wisest beast
The serpent would live forever in the sea
3.correctAnswer: Enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between its offspring and hers; her offspring would crush its head, and it would strike his heel
3.explanation: God said: 'I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.'

3.question: What did the Lord God make for Adam and his wife to replace their fig leaf coverings?
options: Garments of skin (leather) to clothe them
3.correctAnswer: Garments of skin (leather) to clothe them
3.explanation: Genesis 3:21 states: 'The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.'

3.question: What was placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden to guard the way to the Tree of Life after mankind was expelled?
options: A high stone wall and iron gate
Cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth
A ring of roaring desert fires
3.correctAnswer: Cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth
3.explanation: He placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth to guard the way to the Tree of Life.

4.question: What occupations did Cain and Abel have in Genesis 4:2?
options: Abel was a builder, Cain was a metalworker
Abel kept flocks (shepherd), and Cain worked the soil (farmer)
Abel was a fisherman, Cain was a hunter
4.correctAnswer: Abel kept flocks (shepherd), and Cain worked the soil (farmer)
4.explanation: Genesis 4:2 states: 'Now Abel kept flocks, and Cain worked the soil.'

4.question: What offerings did Cain and Abel bring to the Lord?
options: Cain brought silver; Abel brought gold
Cain brought some fruits of the soil; Abel brought fat portions from the firstborn of his flock
Cain brought incense; Abel brought wine
Both brought olive oil and bread
4.correctAnswer: Cain brought some fruits of the soil; Abel brought fat portions from the firstborn of his flock
4.explanation: Cain brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering, but Abel brought fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock.

4.question: How did the Lord respond to the offerings of the two brothers?
options: He looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering He did not look with favor
He commanded them to switch occupations
4.correctAnswer: He looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering He did not look with favor
4.explanation: The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor; so Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.

4.question: What warning did the Lord give Cain regarding sin crouching at the door in Genesis 4:7?
options: 'Sin is harmless if you ignore it'
'Sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it'
'You cannot avoid sin, so give up'
4.correctAnswer: 'Sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it'
4.explanation: God warned Cain: 'If you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it.'

4.question: Where did Cain take Abel when he attacked and murdered him?
4.explanation: Cain said to his brother Abel, 'Let’s go out to the field.' While they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

4.question: How did Cain reply when the Lord asked him, 'Where is your brother Abel?'
options: 'I don't know. Am I my brother’s keeper?'
4.correctAnswer: 'I don't know. Am I my brother’s keeper?'
4.explanation: Cain lied and retorted with defiance: 'I don't know. Am I my brother's keeper?'

4.question: What did God say was crying out to Him from the ground in Genesis 4:10?
options: The blood of Cain's brother Abel
4.correctAnswer: The blood of Cain's brother Abel
4.explanation: The Lord said: 'What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground.'

4.question: What protection did the Lord place upon Cain when he feared he would be killed as a restless wanderer?
options: The Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him
4.correctAnswer: The Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him
4.explanation: The Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him, declaring sevenfold vengeance on anyone who killed Cain.

4.question: To which land did Cain go to live after leaving the presence of the Lord, and what was the name of the city he built?
options: The land of Ur; city of Babylon
The land of Nod, east of Eden; city of Enoch (named after his son)
The land of Canaan; city of Jerusalem
The land of Egypt; city of Memphis
4.correctAnswer: The land of Nod, east of Eden; city of Enoch (named after his son)
4.explanation: Cain lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden. He was then building a city, and he named it after his son Enoch.

4.question: Who was born to Adam and Eve to replace Abel, and what did people begin to do during the time of his son Enosh?
options: Lamech; they began to build towers
Seth; at that time people began to call on the name of the Lord
Tubal-Cain; they began to forge weapons
Jubal; they began to write poetry
4.correctAnswer: Seth; at that time people began to call on the name of the Lord
4.explanation: Eve gave birth to Seth, saying 'God has granted me another child in place of Abel.' To Seth also a son was born named Enosh; at that time people began to call on the name of the Lord.

5.question: How old was Adam when his son Seth was born in his own likeness and image?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:3 states: 'When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Seth.'

5.question: How long did Adam live altogether before he died?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:5 records: 'Altogether, Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.'

5.question: What refrain is repeated throughout Genesis 5 for almost every patriarch after recording their lifespan?
5.explanation: The solemn refrain 'and then he died' emphasizes the reality of physical death entering humanity after the Fall.

5.question: What exceptional testimony is recorded about Enoch in Genesis 5:22 and 5:24?
options: He walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away
He built the first great library
5.correctAnswer: He walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away
5.explanation: Genesis 5:24 states: 'Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away.'

5.question: How long did Enoch live on the earth before God took him?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:23 records: 'Altogether, Enoch lived a total of 365 years.'

5.question: Who was the oldest recorded human in the Bible according to Genesis 5:27, and how old was he?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:27 states: 'Altogether, Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.'

5.question: Who was the father of Methuselah, and who was Methuselah's famous grandson?
options: Adam was father; Seth was grandson
Enoch was father; Noah was grandson
Cain was father; Lamech was grandson
Jared was father; Shem was grandson
5.correctAnswer: Enoch was father; Noah was grandson
5.explanation: Enoch fathered Methuselah, Methuselah fathered Lamech, and Lamech fathered Noah.

5.question: What prophecy did Lamech make when naming his son Noah in Genesis 5:29?
options: 'He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed'
'He will build the tallest tower on earth'
'He will bring wealth from foreign lands'
5.correctAnswer: 'He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed'
5.explanation: Lamech named him Noah ('Rest/Comfort') and said, 'He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed.'

5.question: How old was Lamech when he died, having lived 595 years after Noah was born?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:31 records: 'Altogether, Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.'

5.question: Who were the three sons of Noah listed at the close of Genesis 5?
5.explanation: Genesis 5:32 states: 'After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.'

6.question: What limit did the Lord place on the human lifespan in Genesis 6:3?
6.explanation: The Lord said, 'My Spirit will not contend with humans forever, for they are mortal; their days will be 120 years.'

6.question: Who were the Nephilim mentioned in Genesis 6:4?
options: Heroes of old, men of renown who were on the earth in those days
6.correctAnswer: Heroes of old, men of renown who were on the earth in those days
6.explanation: Genesis 6:4 describes the Nephilim as the heroes of old, men of renown who were on the earth in those days.

6.question: How did the Lord evaluate the human condition in Genesis 6:5?
options: Humans were mostly obedient with small flaws
Every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time
The earth was full of peace
6.correctAnswer: Every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time
6.explanation: The Lord saw how great the wickedness of the human race had become, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time.

6.question: How did the Lord feel about having made human beings on the earth in Genesis 6:6?
options: He was troubled, His heart was deeply troubled, and He regretted having made them
He resolved to create a second moon
6.correctAnswer: He was troubled, His heart was deeply troubled, and He regretted having made them
6.explanation: Genesis 6:6 states: 'The Lord regretted that he had made human beings on the earth, and his heart was deeply troubled.'

6.question: What remarkable statement is made about Noah in Genesis 6:8?
options: Noah was the wealthiest man of his age
Noah found favor (grace) in the eyes of the Lord
Noah had traveled around the entire world
6.correctAnswer: Noah found favor (grace) in the eyes of the Lord
6.explanation: Genesis 6:8 records: 'But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.'

6.question: How does Genesis 6:9 describe Noah's personal character?
options: A righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, who walked faithfully with God
6.correctAnswer: A righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, who walked faithfully with God
6.explanation: Genesis 6:9 says: 'Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God.'

6.question: What type of wood was Noah instructed to use to construct the Ark?
6.explanation: God told Noah: 'Make yourself an ark of gopher wood (cypress wood); make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out.'

6.question: What were the dimensions of the Ark according to Genesis 6:15?
options: 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high
6.correctAnswer: 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high
6.explanation: The Ark was to be 300 cubits long (approx. 450 ft), 50 cubits wide (75 ft), and 30 cubits high (45 ft).

6.question: How many decks (stories) was Noah instructed to build inside the Ark?
options: Three decks: lower, middle, and upper
6.correctAnswer: Three decks: lower, middle, and upper
6.explanation: Genesis 6:16 specifies: 'Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks.'

6.question: How did Noah respond to all of God's instructions in Genesis 6:22?
options: He argued and questioned the dimensions
Noah did everything just as God commanded him
He delayed construction for forty years
He built only half the Ark
6.correctAnswer: Noah did everything just as God commanded him
6.explanation: Genesis 6:22 records: 'Noah did everything just as God commanded him.'

7.question: How many of every kind of clean animal was Noah instructed to take on the Ark?
7.explanation: God commanded: 'Take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate, and one pair of every kind of unclean animal.'

7.question: How old was Noah when the floodwaters came on the earth?
7.explanation: Genesis 7:6 states: 'Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.'

7.question: How many humans entered the Ark in total according to Genesis 7:7 and 7:13?
options: Eight (Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their three wives)
7.correctAnswer: Eight (Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their three wives)
7.explanation: Eight people entered the Ark: Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his wife, and the three wives of his sons.

7.question: What two water sources were opened on the day the Flood began in Genesis 7:11?
options: The rivers of Eden and the Red Sea
All the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened
A tidal wave from the Mediterranean
7.correctAnswer: All the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened
7.explanation: On that day all the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.

7.question: How many days and nights did rain fall upon the earth during the Flood?
7.explanation: Genesis 7:12 states: 'And rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.'

7.question: Who shut the door of the Ark after Noah and the animals entered in Genesis 7:16?
options: Noah with a heavy wooden bar
A powerful wind blew it shut
7.explanation: Genesis 7:16 says: 'The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord shut him in.'

7.question: How high did the floodwaters rise above the highest mountains under the heavens in Genesis 7:20?
7.explanation: Genesis 7:20 records: 'The waters rose and covered the mountains to a depth of more than fifteen cubits.'

7.question: What happened to every living creature on the dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils?
options: Every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out; only Noah and those with him in the ark remained
Many adapted and learned to swim
7.correctAnswer: Every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out; only Noah and those with him in the ark remained
7.explanation: Every living thing that moved on land perished—birds, livestock, wild animals, all creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind.

7.question: For how many days did the floodwaters flood (prevail over) the earth in Genesis 7:24?
7.explanation: Genesis 7:24 states: 'The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.'

7.question: What is the primary spiritual lesson illustrated by God preserving Noah in the Ark?
options: That boats are superior to cities
That God judges persistent wickedness while faithfully saving the righteous who trust and obey Him
7.correctAnswer: That God judges persistent wickedness while faithfully saving the righteous who trust and obey Him
7.explanation: The Flood demonstrates both God's holy justice against global corruption and His covenant mercy in preserving a righteous remnant through the Ark.

8.question: What did God remember at the start of Genesis 8, and what did He send over the earth?
options: God remembered the gold of Eden and sent an earthquake
God remembered Noah and all the animals, and He sent a wind over the earth, causing the waters to recede
God remembered the garden and sent rain
8.correctAnswer: God remembered Noah and all the animals, and He sent a wind over the earth, causing the waters to recede
8.explanation: Genesis 8:1 states: 'But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and the livestock that were with him in the ark, and he sent a wind over the earth, and the waters receded.'

8.question: Where did the Ark come to rest on the seventeenth day of the seventh month?
8.explanation: Genesis 8:4 records: 'and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.'

8.question: Which bird did Noah send out first from the Ark window, and what did it do?
options: A dove; it built a nest on the roof
A raven; it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth
An eagle; it flew to Egypt
8.correctAnswer: A raven; it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth
8.explanation: Noah sent out a raven, and it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.

8.question: Why did the dove return to Noah the first time it was sent out in Genesis 8:9?
options: It was attacked by birds of prey
It could find nowhere to perch because there was water over all the surface of the earth
Noah called it back with a whistle
8.correctAnswer: It could find nowhere to perch because there was water over all the surface of the earth
8.explanation: The dove could find nowhere to perch because there was water over all the surface of the earth; so it returned to Noah in the ark.

8.question: What did the dove bring back in its beak when Noah sent it out the second time seven days later?
8.explanation: When the dove returned to him in the evening, there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.

8.question: What happened when Noah sent the dove out the third time after waiting another seven days?
options: It did not return to him again
It brought a branch of grapes
8.correctAnswer: It did not return to him again
8.explanation: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not return to him.

8.question: What did Noah see when he removed the covering from the Ark on the first day of the first month of his 601st year?
options: The surface of the ground was dry
8.correctAnswer: The surface of the ground was dry
8.explanation: Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

8.question: What was the very first thing Noah built after coming out of the Ark onto dry land?
options: An altar to the Lord, sacrificing burnt offerings of every clean animal and clean bird
8.correctAnswer: An altar to the Lord, sacrificing burnt offerings of every clean animal and clean bird
8.explanation: Then Noah built an altar to the Lord and, taking some of all the clean animals and clean birds, he sacrificed burnt offerings on it.

8.question: How did the Lord respond to Noah's burnt offering on the altar?
options: The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma and said in His heart He would never again curse the ground because of humans
The Lord sent fire to consume the mountain
8.correctAnswer: The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma and said in His heart He would never again curse the ground because of humans
8.explanation: The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart: 'Never again will I curse the ground because of humans, even though every inclination of the human heart is evil from childhood.'

8.question: What perpetual cycle did God promise would never cease as long as the earth endures in Genesis 8:22?
options: Seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night
8.correctAnswer: Seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night
8.explanation: Genesis 8:22 declares: 'As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease.'

9.question: What blessing and commandment did God speak to Noah and his sons in Genesis 9:1?
options: 'Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the earth'
9.correctAnswer: 'Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the earth'
9.explanation: God blessed Noah and his sons, saying to them, 'Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the earth.'

9.question: What change regarding diet was explicitly granted to mankind in Genesis 9:3?
options: Humans could only eat figs and dates
Just as God gave the green plants, He now gave everything that lives and moves as food
Humans were forbidden to eat plants
Meat could only be eaten on feast days
9.correctAnswer: Just as God gave the green plants, He now gave everything that lives and moves as food
9.explanation: God said: 'Everything that lives and moves about will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.'

9.question: What strict dietary restriction was commanded regarding meat in Genesis 9:4?
options: You must not cook it with salt
You must not eat meat that has its lifeblood still in it
You must not eat meat in winter
You must not eat the fat
9.correctAnswer: You must not eat meat that has its lifeblood still in it
9.explanation: Genesis 9:4 commands: 'But you must not eat meat that has its lifeblood still in it.'

9.question: Why does God demand an accounting for human life in Genesis 9:6 ('Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed')?
options: Because in the image of God has God made mankind
Because laws are necessary for trade
9.correctAnswer: Because in the image of God has God made mankind
9.explanation: 'Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed; for in the image of God has God made mankind.'

9.question: With whom did God establish His covenant in Genesis 9:9–10?
options: With Noah, his descendants, and with every living creature that was with him
With the plants of the earth only
9.correctAnswer: With Noah, his descendants, and with every living creature that was with him
9.explanation: God said, 'I now establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you and with every living creature that was with you.'

9.question: What promise is at the heart of the covenant in Genesis 9:11?
options: Never again will all life be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth
That the sun will never set
9.correctAnswer: Never again will all life be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth
9.explanation: God promised: 'Never again will all life be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.'

9.question: What visual sign did God set in the clouds as the token of His everlasting covenant?
9.explanation: God said: 'I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.'

9.question: What did Noah plant, and what unfortunate incident followed in Genesis 9:20–21?
options: An olive grove; he fell from a tree
A vineyard; he drank some of its wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent
Wheat fields; locusts ate the crop
Fig trees; he refused to share with his family
9.correctAnswer: A vineyard; he drank some of its wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent
9.explanation: Noah, a man of the soil, planted a vineyard. When he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered inside his tent.

9.question: How did Shem and Japheth honor their father when Ham told them about his nakedness?
options: They mocked him along with Ham
They took a garment, walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness without looking at him
They carried him out into the rain
9.correctAnswer: They took a garment, walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness without looking at him
9.explanation: Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it across their shoulders; then they walked backward and covered their father’s naked body, keeping their faces turned away.

9.question: How many years did Noah live in total before he died?
9.explanation: After the flood Noah lived 350 years. Altogether, Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.

10.question: What is the common title given to the historical record in Genesis Chapter 10?
options: The Book of the Wars of the Lord
The Table of Nations (generations of Noah's sons)
10.correctAnswer: The Table of Nations (generations of Noah's sons)
10.explanation: Genesis 10 is traditionally known as the Table of Nations, listing the descendants of Shem, Ham, and Japheth through whom the nations spread after the Flood.

10.question: Which son of Noah is associated with maritime coastland peoples such as Gomer, Magog, Madai, and Javan?
10.explanation: From the sons of Japheth (Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshek, and Tiras) maritime peoples spread out into their territories by their clans within their nations.

10.question: Who were the four primary sons of Ham listed in Genesis 10:6?
10.explanation: The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt (Mizraim), Put, and Canaan.

10.question: Who was Nimrod, and how is he famously described in Genesis 10:8–9?
options: A humble shepherd in the desert
A mighty warrior on the earth and a mighty hunter before the Lord
10.correctAnswer: A mighty warrior on the earth and a mighty hunter before the Lord
10.explanation: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became a mighty warrior on the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the Lord.

10.question: What cities formed the beginning of Nimrod's kingdom in the land of Shinar?
10.explanation: Genesis 10:10 states: 'The first centers of his kingdom were Babylon, Uruk, Akkad and Kalneh, in Shinar.'

10.question: From Nimrod's territory, who went into Assyria and built Nineveh and Calah?
10.explanation: From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah and Resen.

10.question: What infamous cities were included within the borders of the Canaanite clans in Genesis 10:19?
options: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha
10.correctAnswer: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha
10.explanation: The borders of Canaan reached from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

10.question: Which son of Noah is designated as the ancestor of all the sons of Eber (the Semites/Hebrews)?
10.explanation: Sons were also born to Shem, whose older brother was Japheth; Shem was the ancestor of all the sons of Eber.

10.question: Why was Eber's son named Peleg in Genesis 10:25?
options: Because he was a mighty archer
Because in his days the earth was divided
Because he built a great altar
Because he lived near the sea
10.correctAnswer: Because in his days the earth was divided
10.explanation: One son was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided; his brother was named Joktan.

10.question: How many total nation groups/clans are traditionally identified as originating from Noah's sons in Genesis 10?
10.explanation: Genesis 10 enumerates 70 nations (14 Japhethite, 30 Hamitic, 26 Semitic), representing the totality of ancient post-flood humanity.

11.question: What was the linguistic state of the whole world at the opening of Genesis 11?
options: Each tribe had its own distinct language
The whole world had one language and a common speech
Writing had not yet been invented
11.correctAnswer: The whole world had one language and a common speech
11.explanation: Genesis 11:1 states: 'Now the whole world had one language and a common speech.'

11.question: Where did the people settle as they journeyed eastward?
options: On a plain in the land of Shinar (Babylonia)
11.correctAnswer: On a plain in the land of Shinar (Babylonia)
11.explanation: As people moved eastward, they found a plain in Shinar and settled there.

11.question: What building materials did the people use instead of stone and mortar?
options: Hewn cedar beams and iron nails
Bricks baked thoroughly, and tar (bitumen) for mortar
11.correctAnswer: Bricks baked thoroughly, and tar (bitumen) for mortar
11.explanation: They said, 'Come, let’s make bricks and bake them thoroughly.' They used brick instead of stone, and tar for mortar.

11.question: What twofold objective did the builders declare in Genesis 11:4?
options: To explore the ocean and discover new lands
To build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered
To build a tomb for Nimrod
11.correctAnswer: To build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered
11.explanation: They said, 'Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of the whole earth.'

11.question: What did the Lord do in response to the city and tower human beings were building?
options: He sent fire and destroyed the tower
He came down to see it, confused their language so they could not understand each other, and scattered them over the earth
He appointed a king over them
He sent angels to finish the construction
11.correctAnswer: He came down to see it, confused their language so they could not understand each other, and scattered them over the earth
11.explanation: The Lord came down, confused their language so they could not understand each other, and scattered them from there over all the earth.

11.question: Why was the city named Babel in Genesis 11:9?
options: Because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world
Because it was built by Nimrod
Because it was high in altitude
11.correctAnswer: Because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world
11.explanation: That is why it was called Babel—because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world.

11.question: Who was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran in the genealogy of Shem?
11.explanation: After Terah had lived 70 years, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

11.question: Who was Lot in relation to Abram according to Genesis 11:27–31?
options: Abram's nephew (the son of Abram's deceased brother Haran)
11.correctAnswer: Abram's nephew (the son of Abram's deceased brother Haran)
11.explanation: Haran became the father of Lot; when Haran died in Ur, Lot was Abram's nephew.

11.question: What vital detail is recorded about Sarai when she is first introduced in Genesis 11:30?
options: Now Sarai was childless because she was not able to conceive (barren)
11.correctAnswer: Now Sarai was childless because she was not able to conceive (barren)
11.explanation: Genesis 11:30 explicitly notes: 'Now Sarai was childless because she was not able to conceive.'

11.question: From which city did Terah set out, and in which city did he settle and die at age 205?
options: Left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan, but settled in Haran and died there
11.correctAnswer: Left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan, but settled in Haran and died there
11.explanation: Terah took Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan, but when they came to Haran, they settled there, and Terah died in Haran at 205.

12.question: What call did the Lord give to Abram in Genesis 12:1?
options: 'Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you'
12.correctAnswer: 'Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you'
12.explanation: The Lord said to Abram: 'Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you.'

12.question: What universal promise did God attach to the blessing of Abram in Genesis 12:3?
options: 'All peoples on earth will be blessed through you'
12.correctAnswer: 'All peoples on earth will be blessed through you'
12.explanation: God declared: 'I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.'

12.question: How old was Abram when he departed from Haran in obedience to the Lord?
12.explanation: Genesis 12:4 records: 'Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Haran.'

12.question: Where did Abram build his first altar in Canaan after the Lord appeared to him saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land'?
options: At the great tree of Moreh at Shechem
12.correctAnswer: At the great tree of Moreh at Shechem
12.explanation: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the great tree of Moreh at Shechem. There the Lord appeared to him, and he built an altar.

12.question: Between which two locations did Abram pitch his tent and build his second altar, calling on the name of the Lord?
options: Between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east
12.correctAnswer: Between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east
12.explanation: He moved on toward the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar and called on the name of the Lord.

12.question: Why did Abram go down to Egypt in Genesis 12:10?
options: Because there was a severe famine in the land of Canaan
12.correctAnswer: Because there was a severe famine in the land of Canaan
12.explanation: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.

12.question: What did Abram ask Sarai to say when entering Egypt, and why?
options: To say she was a prophetess to gain respect
To say she was his sister, so that he would be treated well and his life spared because of her beauty
To disguise herself in beggar's clothes
To stay behind in the desert
12.correctAnswer: To say she was his sister, so that he would be treated well and his life spared because of her beauty
12.explanation: Abram feared the Egyptians would kill him because of Sarai's beauty, so he asked her to say: 'Say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake and my life will be spared.'

12.question: What happened to Sarai after Egyptian officials praised her beauty to Pharaoh?
options: She was taken into Pharaoh’s palace
She was sent back to Haran
12.correctAnswer: She was taken into Pharaoh’s palace
12.explanation: When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful, and she was taken into Pharaoh's palace.

12.question: How did the Lord intervene to protect Sarai and prevent Pharaoh from touching her?
options: The Lord sent an angel with a flaming sword to guard the gate
The Lord inflicted serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Abram's wife Sarai
The Lord caused an earthquake in Egypt
The Lord dried up the Nile river
12.correctAnswer: The Lord inflicted serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Abram's wife Sarai
12.explanation: Genesis 12:17 states: 'But the Lord inflicted serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Abram’s wife Sarai.'

12.question: What did Pharaoh do when he discovered that Sarai was actually Abram's wife?
options: He summoned Abram, rebuked him for not telling the truth, and gave orders to send him and his wife away with all they had
He made Abram his chief minister
12.correctAnswer: He summoned Abram, rebuked him for not telling the truth, and gave orders to send him and his wife away with all they had
12.explanation: Pharaoh asked, 'What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?' Then Pharaoh gave orders about Abram to his men, and they sent him on his way with his wife and everything he had.

13.question: How does Genesis 13:2 describe Abram's material wealth upon coming up from Egypt?
options: He had lost all his possessions
Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold
He had only a few donkeys
13.correctAnswer: Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold
13.explanation: Genesis 13:2 states: 'Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold.'

13.question: To which exact place did Abram return to worship and call upon the name of the Lord?
options: The place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been earlier and where he had first built an altar
13.correctAnswer: The place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been earlier and where he had first built an altar
13.explanation: He returned to the place between Bethel and Ai where he had first built an altar, and there Abram called on the name of the Lord.

13.question: Why could the land not support Abram and Lot dwelling together in Genesis 13:6?
options: Their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together
A sudden flood ruined the pastures
13.correctAnswer: Their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together
13.explanation: The land could not support them while they stayed together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together.

13.question: What problem arose between their respective camps in Genesis 13:7?
options: Quarreling arose between Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders
13.correctAnswer: Quarreling arose between Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders
13.explanation: Quarreling arose between Abram's herders and Lot's herders; the Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.

13.question: What generous proposal did Abram make to Lot to prevent conflict?
options: 'Let us flip a coin for the land'
'Let’s not have any quarreling between you and me... Is not the whole land before you? Let’s part company. If you go to the left, I’ll go to the right; if you go to the right, I’ll go to the left.'
'I am the elder, so I will take the best'
13.correctAnswer: 'Let’s not have any quarreling between you and me... Is not the whole land before you? Let’s part company. If you go to the left, I’ll go to the right; if you go to the right, I’ll go to the left.'
13.explanation: Abram graciously gave the younger nephew first choice: 'If you go to the left, I’ll go to the right; if you go to the right, I’ll go to the left.'

13.question: What did Lot see when he looked around at the plain of the Jordan in Genesis 13:10?
options: The whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt toward Zoar
13.correctAnswer: The whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt toward Zoar
13.explanation: Lot looked around and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan toward Zoar was well watered, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt (before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah).

13.question: Which direction and location did Lot choose, and near which infamous city did he pitch his tents?
options: He chose the western sea and pitched tents near Tyre
He chose the whole plain of the Jordan, journeyed east, and pitched his tents near Sodom
He chose the Negev desert near Beersheba
He chose the hills of Shechem
13.correctAnswer: He chose the whole plain of the Jordan, journeyed east, and pitched his tents near Sodom
13.explanation: Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and set out toward the east. He lived among the cities of the plain and pitched his tents near Sodom.

13.question: What notable description is given of the inhabitants of Sodom in Genesis 13:13?
options: The people of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord
They were great builders of walls
They lived as hermits in caves
13.correctAnswer: The people of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord
13.explanation: Genesis 13:13 notes: 'Now the people of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord.'

13.question: What did the Lord promise to Abram after Lot had parted from him in Genesis 13:14–16?
options: That he would become a king in Egypt
To give all the land he could see (north, south, east, west) to him and his offspring forever, and make his offspring like the dust of the earth
To give him silver mines in the hills
That Lot would return within a year
13.correctAnswer: To give all the land he could see (north, south, east, west) to him and his offspring forever, and make his offspring like the dust of the earth
13.explanation: God said: 'Look around from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west. All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever. I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth.'

13.question: Where did Abram move his tents, and where did he build an altar to the Lord in Genesis 13:18?
options: Near the city gates of Bethel
Near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron
13.correctAnswer: Near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron
13.explanation: So Abram went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he pitched his tents. There he built an altar to the Lord.

14.question: How many kings from the east fought against five kings of the plains of the Jordan?
options: Four kings (led by Chedorlaomer) against five kings (including Sodom and Gomorrah)
14.correctAnswer: Four kings (led by Chedorlaomer) against five kings (including Sodom and Gomorrah)
14.explanation: Four eastern kings fought against five kings of the Valley of Siddim (including Bera king of Sodom and Birsha king of Gomorrah).

14.question: What was the Valley of Siddim full of, which trapped the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah during their retreat?
14.explanation: The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and when the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some of the men fell into them.

14.question: Who was carried off as a captive when the four victorious eastern kings looted Sodom?
options: Abram's nephew Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom
14.correctAnswer: Abram's nephew Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom
14.explanation: They also carried off Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom.

14.question: How many trained men born in his household did Abram summon to rescue Lot?
14.explanation: Genesis 14:14 states: 'When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and went in pursuit as far as Dan.'

14.question: How far north did Abram and his men pursue the enemy force to rescue the captives?
options: As far as Dan, and north of Damascus to Hobah
As far as the Euphrates river
14.correctAnswer: As far as Dan, and north of Damascus to Hobah
14.explanation: Abram divided his men by night, attacked them, routed them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.

14.question: What did Abram successfully recover after defeating Chedorlaomer and his allied kings?
options: All the goods, his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people
14.correctAnswer: All the goods, his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people
14.explanation: He recovered all the goods and brought back his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people.

14.question: Who came out to meet Abram in the Valley of Shaveh, and what two titles did he hold?
options: Pharaoh, king of Egypt and builder of pyramids
Melchizedek king of Salem and priest of God Most High (El Elyon)
Nimrod, king of Babel and mighty hunter
Abimelech, king of Gerar and judge
14.correctAnswer: Melchizedek king of Salem and priest of God Most High (El Elyon)
14.explanation: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.

14.question: What blessing did Melchizedek pronounce over Abram?
options: 'Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. And praise be to God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand.'
14.correctAnswer: 'Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. And praise be to God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand.'
14.explanation: Melchizedek blessed Abram, saying: 'Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. And praise be to God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand.'

14.question: What did Abram give to Melchizedek following the blessing in Genesis 14:20?
14.explanation: Genesis 14:20 records: 'Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.'

14.question: Why did Abram refuse the king of Sodom's offer to keep the recovered goods?
options: Because he had already lost them
He had sworn an oath to God Most High that he would accept not even a thread or thong of a sandal, lest Sodom claim 'I made Abram rich'
Because he wanted twice as much
14.correctAnswer: He had sworn an oath to God Most High that he would accept not even a thread or thong of a sandal, lest Sodom claim 'I made Abram rich'
14.explanation: Abram said to the king of Sodom: 'I have raised my hand to the Lord, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth, and have taken an oath that I will accept nothing belonging to you, not even a thread or the strap of a sandal, so that you will never be able to say, I made Abram rich.'

15.question: What encouraging words did the Lord speak to Abram in a vision in Genesis 15:1?
options: 'Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.'
15.correctAnswer: 'Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.'
15.explanation: The word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision: 'Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.'

15.question: What concern did Abram express regarding an heir in Genesis 15:2–3?
options: That he had too many children
That he remained childless and a servant in his household, Eliezer of Damascus, would be his heir
15.correctAnswer: That he remained childless and a servant in his household, Eliezer of Damascus, would be his heir
15.explanation: Abram said, 'Sovereign Lord, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?'

15.question: Where did the Lord take Abram, and what comparison was made regarding his future offspring?
options: To the seashore; like the grains of sand
He took him outside and said: 'Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them... So shall your offspring be.'
To a forest; like the leaves
To a river; like the drops of water
15.correctAnswer: He took him outside and said: 'Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them... So shall your offspring be.'
15.explanation: He took him outside and said, 'Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.' Then he said to him, 'So shall your offspring be.'

15.question: What monumental declaration of faith and justification is recorded in Genesis 15:6?
options: Abram doubted the word of the Lord
Abram believed the Lord, and He credited it to him as righteousness
Abram sacrificed an ox to prove his faith
15.correctAnswer: Abram believed the Lord, and He credited it to him as righteousness
15.explanation: Genesis 15:6 is one of the pivotal verses of Scripture: 'Abram believed the Lord, and he credited it to him as righteousness.'

15.question: Which animals did Abram prepare and cut in half for the ancient covenant ceremony?
options: A bull, a horse, and a camel
A heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon
15.correctAnswer: A heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon
15.explanation: God commanded: 'Bring me a heifer, a goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon.' Abram cut them in two and arranged the halves opposite each other.

15.question: What did Abram do when birds of prey came down on the covenant carcasses in Genesis 15:11?
options: He offered them to the birds
He ran back to his tent
15.explanation: Genesis 15:11 states: 'Then birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.'

15.question: What came over Abram as the sun was setting in Genesis 15:12?
options: A deep sleep fell on Abram, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him
15.correctAnswer: A deep sleep fell on Abram, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him
15.explanation: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him.

15.question: What prophecy did the Lord give regarding Abram's descendants in a foreign land in Genesis 15:13–14?
options: They would rule that nation immediately
They would be strangers in a country not their own, enslaved and mistreated four hundred years, but God would punish that nation and they would leave with great possessions
They would forget their God completely
They would perish in the desert
15.correctAnswer: They would be strangers in a country not their own, enslaved and mistreated four hundred years, but God would punish that nation and they would leave with great possessions
15.explanation: God foretold the Egyptian bondage: 'for four hundred years your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own and that they will be enslaved and mistreated there. But I will punish the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.'

15.question: What passed between the divided animal pieces when the sun set and darkness fell in Genesis 15:17?
options: A smoking firepot with a blazing torch (representing God sealing the covenant alone)
15.correctAnswer: A smoking firepot with a blazing torch (representing God sealing the covenant alone)
15.explanation: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces, ratifying the unconditional covenant.

15.question: What were the geographic boundaries of the Promised Land confirmed by the covenant in Genesis 15:18?
options: From the Wadi (River) of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates
From the Jordan river to the Mediterranean Sea
Around the city of Hebron only
15.correctAnswer: From the Wadi (River) of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates
15.explanation: On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram and said: 'To your descendants I give this land, from the Wadi of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.'

16.question: Who was Sarai's Egyptian slave whom she gave to Abram to bear children?
16.explanation: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had an Egyptian slave named Hagar. She said to Abram, 'Go, sleep with my slave; perhaps I can build a family through her.'

16.question: How long had Abram been living in Canaan when Sarai gave Hagar to him as a wife?
16.explanation: Genesis 16:3 specifies: 'After Abram had been living in Canaan ten years, Sarai his wife took her Egyptian slave Hagar and gave her to her husband to be his wife.'

16.question: What attitude did Hagar develop toward Sarai when she realized she had conceived?
options: She began to despise her mistress
She ran away immediately to Egypt
16.correctAnswer: She began to despise her mistress
16.explanation: When Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.

16.question: What did Hagar do when Sarai mistreated her with Abram's permission?
options: She appealed to the elders of Hebron
Hagar fled from Sarai into the desert
She locked herself in her tent
16.correctAnswer: Hagar fled from Sarai into the desert
16.explanation: Genesis 16:6 states: 'Then Sarai mistreated Hagar; so she fled from her.'

16.question: Where did the Angel of the Lord find Hagar in Genesis 16:7?
options: Near a spring in the desert, beside the road to Shur
On the summit of Mount Sinai
16.correctAnswer: Near a spring in the desert, beside the road to Shur
16.explanation: The angel of the Lord found Hagar near a spring in the desert; it was the spring that is beside the road to Shur.

16.question: What instruction did the Angel of the Lord give to Hagar in Genesis 16:9?
options: 'Go on to Egypt and never look back'
'Go back to your mistress and submit to her'
16.correctAnswer: 'Go back to your mistress and submit to her'
16.explanation: Then the angel of the Lord told her, 'Go back to your mistress and submit to her.'

16.question: What name did the Angel tell Hagar to give her unborn son, and why?
options: Ishmael ('God hears'), for the Lord had heard of her misery
Esau, because he would be hairy
16.correctAnswer: Ishmael ('God hears'), for the Lord had heard of her misery
16.explanation: The angel of the Lord said: 'You shall name him Ishmael, for the Lord has heard of your misery.'

16.question: How did the Angel describe Ishmael's future character and life in Genesis 16:12?
options: A quiet farmer in the valleys
A wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone’s hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers
16.correctAnswer: A wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone’s hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers
16.explanation: 'He will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone’s hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.'

16.question: What name did Hagar give to the Lord who spoke to her, and what was the well named?
options: El-Roi ('You are the God who sees me'); the well was called Beer-lahai-roi
16.correctAnswer: El-Roi ('You are the God who sees me'); the well was called Beer-lahai-roi
16.explanation: She gave this name to the Lord who spoke to her: 'You are the God who sees me.' That is why the well was called Beer-lahai-roi ('well of the Living One who sees me').

16.question: How old was Abram when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael?
16.explanation: Genesis 16:16 records: 'Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.'

17.question: How did God reveal Himself to Abram when Abram was ninety-nine years old?
options: 'I am the Creator of the seas'
'I am God Almighty (El Shaddai); walk before me faithfully and be blameless'
17.correctAnswer: 'I am God Almighty (El Shaddai); walk before me faithfully and be blameless'
17.explanation: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said: 'I am God Almighty; walk before me faithfully and be blameless.'

17.question: Why did God change Abram's name ('exalted father') to Abraham in Genesis 17:5?
options: Because he had won a battle
For I have made you a father of many nations
17.correctAnswer: For I have made you a father of many nations
17.explanation: 'No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.'

17.question: What physical sign was established as the everlasting covenant mark for all males throughout generations?
options: Circumcision of every male child at eight days old
17.correctAnswer: Circumcision of every male child at eight days old
17.explanation: God commanded: 'Every male among you shall be circumcised... For the generations to come every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised.'

17.question: What was the consequence for any uncircumcised male according to Genesis 17:14?
options: He had to pay a fine
He will be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant
17.correctAnswer: He will be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant
17.explanation: 'Any uncircumcised male, who has not been circumcised in the flesh, will be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.'

17.question: To what did God change Sarai's name, and what promise did He make concerning her?
options: To Rebecca; she will be a queen
To Sarah ('princess'); I will bless her and give you a son by her; kings of peoples will come from her
To Rachel; she will travel far
To Miriam; she will lead singing
17.correctAnswer: To Sarah ('princess'); I will bless her and give you a son by her; kings of peoples will come from her
17.explanation: God said: 'As for Sarai your wife, you are no longer to call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah. I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her.'

17.question: What was Abraham's internal reaction when God promised a son through ninety-year-old Sarah?
options: Abraham fell facedown, laughed, and said to himself: 'Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at the age of ninety?'
He ran outside shouting with pride
17.correctAnswer: Abraham fell facedown, laughed, and said to himself: 'Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at the age of ninety?'
17.explanation: Abraham fell facedown; he laughed and said to himself, 'Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at the age of ninety?'

17.question: What petition did Abraham plead on behalf of Ishmael in Genesis 17:18?
options: 'If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!'
'Let Ishmael inherit the entire land of Canaan'
17.correctAnswer: 'If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!'
17.explanation: And Abraham said to God, 'If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!'

17.question: What name did God specify for the promised son through Sarah, and with whom would the covenant be established?
options: Isaac ('he laughs'); God would establish His everlasting covenant with Isaac and his descendants
Benjamin; with the tribe of Judah
17.correctAnswer: Isaac ('he laughs'); God would establish His everlasting covenant with Isaac and his descendants
17.explanation: God said, 'Yes, but your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you will call him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant.'

17.question: What specific blessing did God pronounce regarding Ishmael in Genesis 17:20?
options: He would build the city of Jerusalem
He will be fruitful, the father of twelve rulers (princes), and God will make him into a great nation
He would be a priest in Hebron
17.correctAnswer: He will be fruitful, the father of twelve rulers (princes), and God will make him into a great nation
17.explanation: 'And as for Ishmael, I have heard you: I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and will greatly increase his numbers. He will be the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.'

17.question: When did Abraham obey God's command to circumcise himself, his son Ishmael (age 13), and all males of his house?
options: On that very day, as God had told him
17.correctAnswer: On that very day, as God had told him
17.explanation: Genesis 17:23 records: 'On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household... and circumcised them, as God told him.' Abraham was 99 and Ishmael was 13.

18.question: Where was Abraham sitting when the Lord appeared to him near the great trees of Mamre?
options: On a mountain summit at sunrise
Sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day
Inside the city gates of Hebron
18.correctAnswer: Sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day
18.explanation: The Lord appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day.

18.question: What did Abraham do when he looked up and saw three men standing nearby?
options: He hid inside his tent in fear
He hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them, bowed low to the ground, and offered hospitality
He demanded to know their tribe
18.correctAnswer: He hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them, bowed low to the ground, and offered hospitality
18.explanation: When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground, offering water to wash their feet and food to refresh them.

18.question: What meal did Abraham and Sarah quickly prepare for their three visitors?
options: Freshly baked bread from fine flour, curds, milk, and a tender, choice calf
18.correctAnswer: Freshly baked bread from fine flour, curds, milk, and a tender, choice calf
18.explanation: Sarah made bread from three seahs of fine flour, while a servant prepared a choice tender calf, served with curds and milk under a tree while they ate.

18.question: What promise did the Lord state regarding Sarah while the visitors were eating?
options: 'Sarah will live to be two hundred'
'I will return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son'
'Sarah will inherit the fields of Mamre'
'Sarah will become a prophetess in Egypt'
18.correctAnswer: 'I will return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son'
18.explanation: One of them said, 'I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son.'

18.question: What was Sarah's reaction behind the tent entrance, and why?
options: Sarah laughed to herself, thinking, 'After I am worn out and my lord is old, will I now have this pleasure?'
She ran out to thank the visitors
18.correctAnswer: Sarah laughed to herself, thinking, 'After I am worn out and my lord is old, will I now have this pleasure?'
18.explanation: Abraham and Sarah were already very old, and Sarah was past the age of childbearing, so she laughed to herself.

18.question: What rhetorical question did the Lord ask in Genesis 18:14 in response to Sarah's laughter?
options: 'Is anything too hard for the Lord?'
'Do you not know who I am?'
18.correctAnswer: 'Is anything too hard for the Lord?'
18.explanation: Genesis 18:14 declares: 'Is anything too hard for the Lord? I will return to you at the appointed time next year, and Sarah will have a son.'

18.question: Toward which city did the men look as they prepared to leave, prompting the Lord to confide in Abraham?
18.explanation: The men got up and looked down toward Sodom. The Lord said, 'Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?'

18.question: Why had the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah come before the Lord in Genesis 18:20?
options: Because the outcry against them is so great and their sin is so grievous
Because they refused to trade with Egypt
18.correctAnswer: Because the outcry against them is so great and their sin is so grievous
18.explanation: The Lord said, 'The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is so great and their sin so grievous that I will go down and see if what they have done is as bad as the outcry.'

18.question: What foundational biblical principle did Abraham declare when pleading for the city: 'Far be it from you to do such a thing...'
options: 'Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?'
18.correctAnswer: 'Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?'
18.explanation: Abraham pleaded: 'Far be it from you to kill the righteous with the wicked, treating the righteous and the wicked alike. Far be it from you! Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?'

18.question: To what minimum number of righteous people did Abraham intercede before the Lord agreed He would not destroy Sodom for their sake?
18.explanation: Abraham negotiated step by step: 50, 45, 40, 30, 20, down to 10. The Lord answered: 'For the sake of ten, I will not destroy it.'

19.question: Where was Lot sitting when the two angels arrived in Sodom in the evening?
options: In the gateway of the city of Sodom
On the city wall with archers
Outside in the fields grazing sheep
19.correctAnswer: In the gateway of the city of Sodom
19.explanation: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. He got up to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.

19.question: What hospitality did Lot insist upon providing for the two angelic visitors?
options: He directed them to an inn
He urged them strongly to turn aside to his house, wash their feet, eat unleavened bread, and spend the night
He gave them coins to leave the city
He invited all the elders to meet them
19.correctAnswer: He urged them strongly to turn aside to his house, wash their feet, eat unleavened bread, and spend the night
19.explanation: Lot insisted they stay in his house rather than spend the night in the square; he prepared a meal and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.

19.question: Who surrounded Lot's house before they had gone to bed?
options: All the men from every part of the city of Sodom—both young and old
19.correctAnswer: All the men from every part of the city of Sodom—both young and old
19.explanation: Genesis 19:4 notes: 'Before they had gone to bed, all the men from every part of the city of Sodom—both young and old—surrounded the house.'

19.question: How did the angels protect Lot when the mob attempted to break down the door?
options: They reached out, pulled Lot back into the house, shut the door, and struck the men with blindness
They collapsed the roof of the house
19.correctAnswer: They reached out, pulled Lot back into the house, shut the door, and struck the men with blindness
19.explanation: The two men reached out and pulled Lot back into the house and shut the door. Then they struck the men who were at the door with blindness, so they could not find the door.

19.question: How did Lot's sons-in-law react when he warned them that the Lord was about to destroy the city?
19.explanation: Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters: 'Hurry and get out of this place, because the Lord is about to destroy the city!' But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.

19.question: What did the angels do when Lot hesitated at dawn in Genesis 19:16?
options: Because the Lord was merciful to them, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and two daughters and led them safely out of the city
They carried him in a cart
19.correctAnswer: Because the Lord was merciful to them, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and two daughters and led them safely out of the city
19.explanation: When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and of his two daughters and led them safely out of the city, for the Lord was merciful to them.

19.question: To which small town did the angels grant Lot permission to flee instead of the mountains?
19.explanation: Lot pleaded to flee to a nearby small town: 'That is why the town was called Zoar.' The angel told him to hurry there, because he could do nothing until Lot arrived.

19.question: What rained down upon Sodom and Gomorrah from the Lord out of the heavens?
options: Burning sulfur (brimstone and fire) from the Lord out of the heavens
19.correctAnswer: Burning sulfur (brimstone and fire) from the Lord out of the heavens
19.explanation: Then the Lord rained down burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah—from the Lord out of the heavens, completely overthrowing those cities and the entire plain.

19.question: What happened to Lot's wife when she looked back toward Sodom contrary to the angel's command?
options: She looked back, and she became a pillar of salt
She was struck by an arrow
She was carried away by wind
19.correctAnswer: She looked back, and she became a pillar of salt
19.explanation: Genesis 19:26 records: 'But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.'

19.question: What did Abraham see when he looked down toward Sodom, Gomorrah, and all the plain the next morning?
options: A clean desert plain with flowers
Dense smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace
19.correctAnswer: Dense smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace
19.explanation: Abraham went to the place where he had stood before the Lord, looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and saw dense smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace.

20.question: To which region did Abraham move from the area of Mamre, staying between Kadesh and Shur?
20.explanation: Now Abraham moved on from there into the region of the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar.

20.question: What claim did Abraham make concerning his wife Sarah while in Gerar?
20.explanation: And there Abraham said of his wife Sarah, 'She is my sister.'

20.question: Who sent for Sarah and took her into his household in Genesis 20:2?
20.explanation: Genesis 20:2 states: 'Then Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.'

20.question: How did God warn Abimelech regarding Sarah in Genesis 20:3?
options: By sending a prophet with a letter
God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said: 'You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman'
By drying up his water supply
20.correctAnswer: God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said: 'You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman'
20.explanation: God warned Abimelech in a dream: 'You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman.'

20.question: What defense did Abimelech plead before the Lord, since he had not approached Sarah?
options: 'I am king and have right to all women'
'Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation? Did he not say to me, She is my sister... I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands'
20.correctAnswer: 'Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation? Did he not say to me, She is my sister... I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands'
20.explanation: Abimelech had not gone near her, so he said, 'Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation? Did he not say to me, She is my sister, and didn’t she also say, He is my brother? I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands.'

20.question: What did God acknowledge about Abimelech, and what did God reveal He had done?
