options: God knew he did this with a clear conscience, so God kept him from touching her and sinning against Him
God told him to keep Sarah
God said it was too late
20.correctAnswer: God knew he did this with a clear conscience, so God kept him from touching her and sinning against Him
20.explanation: God said: 'Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.'

20.question: What title did God give to Abraham when commanding Abimelech to return his wife in Genesis 20:7?
options: 'He is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live'
20.correctAnswer: 'He is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live'
20.explanation: 'Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live.'

20.question: What reason did Abraham give to Abimelech for concealing that Sarah was his wife?
options: He thought: 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
20.correctAnswer: He thought: 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
20.explanation: Abraham replied, 'I said to myself, There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'

20.question: What familial relationship existed between Abraham and Sarah according to Genesis 20:12?
options: She was his half-sister (daughter of his father, but not of his mother)
They were unrelated strangers from Ur
20.correctAnswer: She was his half-sister (daughter of his father, but not of his mother)
20.explanation: Abraham explained: 'Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father though not of my mother; and she became my wife.'

20.question: What did Abimelech give to Abraham when restoring Sarah, and what happened when Abraham prayed?
options: Sheep, cattle, male and female slaves, 1,000 shekels of silver; and when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech, his wife, and slaves so they could have children
He drove Abraham into the desert
20.correctAnswer: Sheep, cattle, male and female slaves, 1,000 shekels of silver; and when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech, his wife, and slaves so they could have children
20.explanation: Abimelech gave gifts of sheep, cattle, slaves, and 1,000 shekels of silver. Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female slaves so they could have children again, for the Lord had closed up every womb.

21.question: How old was Abraham when his promised son Isaac was born?
21.explanation: Genesis 21:5 records: 'Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.'

21.question: What did Sarah proclaim with joy when Isaac was born in Genesis 21:6?
options: 'God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me'
'No woman has ever suffered like me'
21.correctAnswer: 'God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me'
21.explanation: Sarah said, 'God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.'

21.question: On which day did Abraham circumcise Isaac as God had commanded him?
21.explanation: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him.

21.question: What did Sarah see Ishmael doing on the great day Isaac was weaned?
21.explanation: Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking, which led her to demand their departure.

21.question: What did God instruct Abraham to do when Abraham was distressed over Hagar and Ishmael?
options: To listen to whatever Sarah tells him, for it is through Isaac that his offspring will be reckoned
21.correctAnswer: To listen to whatever Sarah tells him, for it is through Isaac that his offspring will be reckoned
21.explanation: God said to Abraham, 'Do not be so distressed about the boy and your slave. Listen to whatever Sarah tells you, because it is through Isaac that your offspring will be reckoned.'

21.question: What happened to Hagar and the boy when they wandered in the desert of Beersheba and the water was gone?
options: She put the boy under a bush and sat down a bowshot away, weeping so she would not see him die
They found an abandoned oasis immediately
21.correctAnswer: She put the boy under a bush and sat down a bowshot away, weeping so she would not see him die
21.explanation: When the water in the skin was gone, she put the boy under one of the bushes. Then she went off and sat down about a bowshot away, weeping: 'I cannot watch the boy die.'

21.question: How did God intervene to save Hagar and Ishmael in the desert in Genesis 21:17–19?
options: He sent a sudden cloudburst of rain
God heard the boy crying, the Angel spoke from heaven, and God opened her eyes to see a well of water
21.correctAnswer: God heard the boy crying, the Angel spoke from heaven, and God opened her eyes to see a well of water
21.explanation: God heard the boy crying. Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water; she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

21.question: What skill did Ishmael develop as he grew up living in the desert of Paran?
21.explanation: God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became an archer.

21.question: Why did Abraham give seven ewe lambs to King Abimelech at Beersheba?
options: As a witness that Abraham had dug the well of water
21.correctAnswer: As a witness that Abraham had dug the well of water
21.explanation: Abraham said, 'Accept these seven ewes from my hand as a witness that I dug this well.'

21.question: What tree did Abraham plant at Beersheba, where he called on the name of the Lord, the Eternal God?
21.explanation: Genesis 21:33 states: 'Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the Lord, the Eternal God.'

22.question: What test did God give to Abraham at the opening of Genesis 22?
options: To give away all his gold to the poor
'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.'
To leave Canaan and move to Egypt permanently
22.correctAnswer: 'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.'
22.explanation: God tested Abraham, saying: 'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering.'

22.question: On which day of the journey did Abraham look up and see the place in the distance?
22.explanation: Genesis 22:4 states: 'On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.'

22.question: What profound statement of faith did Abraham speak to his servants before ascending the mountain?
options: 'Stay here with the donkey while I and the boy go over there. We will worship and then we will come back to you.'
22.correctAnswer: 'Stay here with the donkey while I and the boy go over there. We will worship and then we will come back to you.'
22.explanation: He said to his servants, 'Stay here with the donkey while I and the boy go over there. We will worship and then we will come back to you.'

22.question: What did Isaac carry up the mountain, and what did Abraham carry in his hand?
options: Isaac carried water; Abraham carried a staff
Isaac carried the wood for the burnt offering, while Abraham carried the fire and the knife
Isaac carried stones; Abraham carried bread
22.correctAnswer: Isaac carried the wood for the burnt offering, while Abraham carried the fire and the knife
22.explanation: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac, and he himself carried the fire and the knife.

22.question: What question did Isaac ask his father as they walked together in Genesis 22:7?
options: 'The fire and wood are here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?'
22.correctAnswer: 'The fire and wood are here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?'
22.explanation: Isaac spoke up and said to his father Abraham, 'Father... the fire and wood are here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?'

22.question: How did Abraham answer Isaac's question in Genesis 22:8?
options: 'We will catch a bird on the hill'
'God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.'
22.correctAnswer: 'God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.'
22.explanation: Abraham answered prophetic words of faith: 'God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.' And the two of them went on together.

22.question: What did the Angel of the Lord call out from heaven just as Abraham reached out his hand with the knife?
options: 'Do not lay a hand on the boy! Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not withheld from me your son, your only son.'
22.correctAnswer: 'Do not lay a hand on the boy! Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not withheld from me your son, your only son.'
22.explanation: The angel of the Lord called from heaven: 'Do not lay a hand on the boy. Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not withheld from me your son, your only son.'

22.question: What substitute sacrifice did Abraham see caught in a thicket by its horns?
22.explanation: Abraham looked up and there in a thicket he saw a ram caught by its horns. He went over, took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son.

22.question: What name did Abraham give to that sacred place in Genesis 22:14?
22.explanation: So Abraham called that place 'The Lord Will Provide' (Jehovah-Jireh). And to this day it is said, 'On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.'

22.question: By what oath did the Lord confirm His covenant with Abraham following this test of obedience?
options: 'I swear by myself, declares the Lord, that because you have done this... I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore'
22.correctAnswer: 'I swear by myself, declares the Lord, that because you have done this... I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore'
22.explanation: The Lord said, 'I swear by myself, declares the Lord, that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son, I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore.'

23.question: How old was Sarah when she died, the only woman whose lifespan is recorded in the Bible?
23.explanation: Genesis 23:1 states: 'Sarah lived to be 127 years old.'

23.question: In which city did Sarah die in the land of Canaan?
23.explanation: She died at Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her.

23.question: How did Abraham identify his legal status when speaking to the Hittite landowners?
options: 'I am a foreigner and a stranger among you'
23.correctAnswer: 'I am a foreigner and a stranger among you'
23.explanation: Abraham addressed the Hittites: 'I am a foreigner and stranger among you. Sell me some property for a burial site here so I can bury my dead.'

23.question: How did the Hittites respectfully address Abraham in Genesis 23:6?
23.explanation: The Hittites replied: 'Sir, listen to us. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs.'

23.question: Which specific cave did Abraham request to purchase as a permanent burial site?
options: The cave of Machpelah, at the end of the field belonging to Ephron son of Zohar
23.correctAnswer: The cave of Machpelah, at the end of the field belonging to Ephron son of Zohar
23.explanation: Abraham asked them to intercede with Ephron son of Zohar so he would sell him the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him and is at the end of his field.

23.question: Where was Ephron sitting when he negotiated with Abraham?
options: Among his people at the gate of his city, in the hearing of all the Hittites
23.correctAnswer: Among his people at the gate of his city, in the hearing of all the Hittites
23.explanation: Ephron the Hittite was sitting among his people and he replied to Abraham in the hearing of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.

23.question: What price did Ephron state for the field and the cave of Machpelah?
options: 400 shekels of silver according to the weight current among merchants
23.correctAnswer: 400 shekels of silver according to the weight current among merchants
23.explanation: Ephron answered: 'Listen to me, my lord; the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver.' Abraham weighed out the four hundred shekels of silver according to the standard current among merchants.

23.question: Why did Abraham insist on paying full commercial value rather than accepting it as an informal gift?
options: To secure legal, undisputed, permanent ownership of the burial site for his family through a public deed
23.correctAnswer: To secure legal, undisputed, permanent ownership of the burial site for his family through a public deed
23.explanation: By weighing the full commercial price at the city gate before all witnesses, Abraham secured the field, the cave, and all trees within its boundaries as an unassailable legal deed.

23.question: What was the significance of the cave of Machpelah in the history of the patriarchs?
options: It became the first parcel of the Promised Land legally owned by Abraham, where Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and Jacob were buried
It was turned into a palace
It was abandoned after Sarah's burial
It was swallowed by an earthquake
23.correctAnswer: It became the first parcel of the Promised Land legally owned by Abraham, where Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and Jacob were buried
23.explanation: The cave of Machpelah near Mamre (Hebron) became the ancestral burying place of the three patriarchal couples: Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob and Leah.

23.question: What virtue does Abraham's conduct in Genesis 23 demonstrate?
options: Integrity, humility, honor, and deep faith in God's promises even in bereavement
23.correctAnswer: Integrity, humility, honor, and deep faith in God's promises even in bereavement
23.explanation: Abraham handled Sarah's passing with profound grief coupled with unwavering integrity, respect for legal customs, and faith that God's land covenant was enduring.

24.question: What oath did Abraham make his senior servant swear by placing his hand under Abraham's thigh?
options: Not to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, but to go to Abraham's country and relatives to find a wife
To give all his wealth to Ishmael
To build a tomb in Ur
24.correctAnswer: Not to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, but to go to Abraham's country and relatives to find a wife
24.explanation: Abraham charged his servant: 'You will not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites... but will go to my country and my own relatives and get a wife for my son Isaac.'

24.question: What did Abraham forbid his servant to do if the woman was unwilling to come back with him?
options: Under no circumstance take Isaac back to the land from which Abraham had come
24.correctAnswer: Under no circumstance take Isaac back to the land from which Abraham had come
24.explanation: Abraham warned: 'Make sure that you do not take my son back there... The Lord God will send his angel before you so that you can get a wife for my son from there.'

24.question: How many camels did the servant take, loaded with all kinds of good things, as he journeyed to Aram Naharaim?
24.explanation: Then the servant left, taking with him ten of his master’s camels loaded with all kinds of good things from his master, and headed for the town of Nahor.

24.question: What specific prayer sign did Abraham's servant request from the Lord at the town well at evening?
options: That the maiden would wear a golden veil
That when he said 'Please lower your jar that I may drink,' the maiden would answer, 'Drink, and I’ll water your camels too'
That lightning would strike a tree
That an elder would introduce her
24.correctAnswer: That when he said 'Please lower your jar that I may drink,' the maiden would answer, 'Drink, and I’ll water your camels too'
24.explanation: The servant prayed: 'May it be that when I say to a young woman, Please let down your jar that I may have a drink, and she says, Drink, and I’ll water your camels too—let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac.'

24.question: Who came out to the well with her jar on her shoulder before the servant had finished praying?
options: Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor
24.correctAnswer: Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor
24.explanation: Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.

24.question: What gifts did the servant present to Rebekah after she watered all ten camels?
options: A roll of linen and a copper bowl
A gold nose ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels
A silver mirror and ivory comb
24.correctAnswer: A gold nose ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels
24.explanation: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels and gave them to her.

24.question: Who was Rebekah's brother who ran out to the spring to welcome the servant after seeing the jewelry?
24.explanation: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he hurried out to the man at the spring after seeing the nose ring and bracelets on his sister.

24.question: What was the conclusion of Laban and Bethuel after hearing the servant recount the providential sign?
options: 'This is from the Lord; we can say nothing to you one way or the other. Here is Rebekah; take her and go'
24.correctAnswer: 'This is from the Lord; we can say nothing to you one way or the other. Here is Rebekah; take her and go'
24.explanation: Laban and Bethuel answered, 'This is from the Lord; we can say nothing to you one way or the other. Here is Rebekah; take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has directed.'

24.question: What was Rebekah's decisive response when her family asked if she would go immediately with the man?
24.explanation: So they called Rebekah and asked her, 'Will you go with this man?' 'I will go,' she said.

24.question: Where was Isaac when Rebekah first saw him, and what was he doing at eventide?
options: He was hunting deer in the mountains
He was out in the field in the evening to meditate (pray)
He was asleep in his tent
24.correctAnswer: He was out in the field in the evening to meditate (pray)
24.explanation: He went out to the field one evening to meditate, and as he looked up, he saw camels approaching. Rebekah veiled herself, Isaac brought her into Sarah's tent, she became his wife, and he loved her.

25.question: Who was the wife Abraham married after Sarah's death, bearing him six sons?
25.explanation: Abraham had taken another wife, whose name was Keturah. She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.

25.question: What did Abraham leave to Isaac, compared to the sons of his concubines?
options: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac; to the sons of his concubines he gave gifts and sent them away to the land of the east
He gave the land to Midian
25.correctAnswer: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac; to the sons of his concubines he gave gifts and sent them away to the land of the east
25.explanation: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac. But while he was still living, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east.

25.question: How old was Abraham when he breathed his last, and where was he buried?
options: 175 years old; in the cave of Machpelah by his sons Isaac and Ishmael
25.correctAnswer: 175 years old; in the cave of Machpelah by his sons Isaac and Ishmael
25.explanation: Abraham lived 175 years. His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron the Hittite, next to Sarah.

25.question: How many tribal rulers (princes) were born to Ishmael according to Genesis 25:16?
25.explanation: These were the sons of Ishmael, twelve tribal rulers according to their settlements and camps. Ishmael lived 137 years.

25.question: What did Isaac do when Rebekah was childless, and how did the Lord answer?
options: Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife, because she was childless. The Lord answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
25.correctAnswer: Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife, because she was childless. The Lord answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
25.explanation: Genesis 25:21 records: 'Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife, because she was childless. The Lord answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.'

25.question: What prophecy did the Lord reveal to Rebekah when the babies jostled each other inside her womb?
options: 'One will be a priest, one a king'
'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.'
25.correctAnswer: 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.'
25.explanation: The Lord said to her: 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.'

25.question: How did the first twin look at birth, and what was he named?
options: Red, his whole body like a hairy garment; they named him Esau ('hairy')
25.correctAnswer: Red, his whole body like a hairy garment; they named him Esau ('hairy')
25.explanation: The first to come out was red, and his whole body was like a hairy garment; so they named him Esau.

25.question: How was the second twin born, and what was he named?
options: His hand grasping Esau’s heel; so he was named Jacob ('he grasps the heel / deceiver')
25.correctAnswer: His hand grasping Esau’s heel; so he was named Jacob ('he grasps the heel / deceiver')
25.explanation: After this, his brother came out, with his hand grasping Esau’s heel; so he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them.

25.question: How did the boys differ in personality and parental affection in Genesis 25:27–28?
options: Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, loved by Isaac (wild game); Jacob was content to stay at home among the tents, loved by Rebekah
Jacob was a warrior; Esau was a scholar
Esau lived in cities; Jacob lived in caves
25.correctAnswer: Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, loved by Isaac (wild game); Jacob was content to stay at home among the tents, loved by Rebekah
25.explanation: The boys grew up: Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was content to stay at home among the tents. Isaac loved Esau because he had a taste for wild game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

25.question: What did Esau sell to Jacob for bread and some red lentil stew when he came in famished from the open country?
options: His birthright (firstborn spiritual and material inheritance)
25.correctAnswer: His birthright (firstborn spiritual and material inheritance)
25.explanation: Jacob said, 'Sell me your birthright.' Esau said, 'I am about to die; what good is the birthright to me?' He swore an oath, selling his birthright to Jacob. 'So Esau despised his birthright.'

26.question: What did the Lord instruct Isaac during the famine in Genesis 26:2?
options: 'Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land where I tell you to live'
26.correctAnswer: 'Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land where I tell you to live'
26.explanation: The Lord appeared to Isaac and said: 'Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land where I tell you to live.'

26.question: What did Isaac claim about Rebekah to the men of Gerar?
26.explanation: When the men of that place asked him about his wife, he said, 'She is my sister,' because he was afraid to say, 'She is my wife.'

26.question: How did King Abimelech discover that Rebekah was actually Isaac's wife?
options: He looked down from a window and saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah
A servant brought a marriage document
26.correctAnswer: He looked down from a window and saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah
26.explanation: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from a window and saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.

26.question: What agricultural miracle happened when Isaac planted crops in that land during the famine year?
options: Isaac planted crops in that land and the same year reaped a hundredfold, because the Lord blessed him
26.correctAnswer: Isaac planted crops in that land and the same year reaped a hundredfold, because the Lord blessed him
26.explanation: Genesis 26:12 states: 'Isaac planted crops in that land and the same year reaped a hundredfold, because the Lord blessed him.'

26.question: Why did the Philistines envy Isaac and stop up all the wells dug in the days of his father Abraham?
options: Because his wealth, flocks, herds, and household grew so large that they envied him and feared his power
26.correctAnswer: Because his wealth, flocks, herds, and household grew so large that they envied him and feared his power
26.explanation: The Philistines envied him. So all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the time of his father Abraham, the Philistines stopped up, filling them with earth.

26.question: What name did Isaac give to the first well where the herders of Gerar quarreled, saying 'The water is ours'?
26.explanation: The herders of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herders and said, 'The water is ours!' So he named the well Esek, because they disputed with him.

26.question: What name did Isaac give to the second well they dug, over which they quarreled also?
26.explanation: Then they dug another well, but they quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.

26.question: What name did Isaac give to the third well when no one quarreled over it, and what did he declare?
options: Rehoboth ('room'), saying: 'Now the Lord has given us room and we will flourish in the land.'
26.correctAnswer: Rehoboth ('room'), saying: 'Now the Lord has given us room and we will flourish in the land.'
26.explanation: He moved on from there and dug another well, and no one quarreled over it. He named it Rehoboth, saying, 'Now the Lord has given us room and we will flourish in the land.'

26.question: Where did Isaac go next, where the Lord appeared to him that night and where he built an altar and pitched his tent?
26.explanation: From there he went up to Beersheba. That night the Lord appeared to him and said, 'I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you.' Isaac built an altar there.

26.question: What grief of mind did Esau bring to his parents Isaac and Rebekah at age forty in Genesis 26:34–35?
options: He married two Hittite women (Judith and Basemath), who were a source of bitterness to Isaac and Rebekah
26.correctAnswer: He married two Hittite women (Judith and Basemath), who were a source of bitterness to Isaac and Rebekah
26.explanation: When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith and Basemath, daughters of Hittites. They were a source of grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

27.question: What physical ailment afflicted elderly Isaac when he called Esau to bless him?
options: He was lame in both feet
His eyes were so weak that he could no longer see (blind)
27.correctAnswer: His eyes were so weak that he could no longer see (blind)
27.explanation: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called for Esau his older son.

27.question: What did Isaac ask Esau to prepare for him before giving him his soul's blessing?
options: Tasty food (savory meat) made from wild game, such as he loved
27.correctAnswer: Tasty food (savory meat) made from wild game, such as he loved
27.explanation: Isaac said: 'Take your quiver and bow, and go out to the open country to hunt some wild game for me. Prepare for me the kind of tasty food I like and bring it to me to eat, so that I may give you my blessing before I die.'

27.question: Who overheard Isaac speaking to Esau and devised a scheme for Jacob to receive the blessing instead?
27.explanation: Now Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to his son Esau, and she instructed Jacob on how to secure the blessing.

27.question: What two young animals did Jacob bring from the flock for Rebekah to prepare tasty food?
27.explanation: Rebekah said: 'Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so I can prepare some tasty food for your father, just the way he likes it.'

27.question: How did Rebekah disguise Jacob so that blind Isaac would think he was hairy Esau?
options: She put Esau's best clothes on him and covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the skins of the young goats
She painted his skin with brown dye
27.correctAnswer: She put Esau's best clothes on him and covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the skins of the young goats
27.explanation: She took the best clothes of Esau and put them on Jacob, and she covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the goatskins.

27.question: What perceptive doubt did Isaac express when touching Jacob in Genesis 27:22?
options: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.'
27.correctAnswer: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.'
27.explanation: Jacob went close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.'

27.question: What was the core promise of the patriarchal blessing Isaac bestowed upon Jacob?
options: May you conquer the lands of Egypt
'May God give you heaven’s dew and earth’s richness—an abundance of grain and new wine. May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you... Blessed be those who bless you!'
May you live in peace without ever traveling
May you build great cities on the coast
27.correctAnswer: 'May God give you heaven’s dew and earth’s richness—an abundance of grain and new wine. May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you... Blessed be those who bless you!'
27.explanation: Isaac blessed him with the dew of heaven, richness of the earth, dominion over his brothers and nations, and divine blessing on those who bless him.

27.question: What was Esau's agonizing reaction when he arrived with his game and discovered Jacob had taken the blessing?
options: He burst out with a loud and bitter cry, weeping and pleading: 'Bless me—me too, my father!'
He left quietly without a word
27.correctAnswer: He burst out with a loud and bitter cry, weeping and pleading: 'Bless me—me too, my father!'
27.explanation: When Esau heard his father’s words, he burst out with a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, 'Bless me—me too, my father!'

27.question: What deadly threat did Esau harbor in his heart against Jacob in Genesis 27:41?
options: 'The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob.'
To report him to the Hittite kings
27.correctAnswer: 'The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob.'
27.explanation: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. He said to himself, 'The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob.'

27.question: Where did Rebekah instruct Jacob to flee to escape Esau's fury?
options: To Egypt to hide in Pharaoh's palace
To her brother Laban in Haran until his brother’s fury subsided
27.correctAnswer: To her brother Laban in Haran until his brother’s fury subsided
27.explanation: Rebekah told Jacob: 'Flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran. Stay with him for a while until your brother’s fury subsides.'

28.question: What charge did Isaac give Jacob before sending him away to Paddan Aram?
options: 'Do not marry a Canaanite woman. Go at once to Paddan Aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel. Take a wife for yourself there, from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.'
'Live as a hunter in the wilderness'
28.correctAnswer: 'Do not marry a Canaanite woman. Go at once to Paddan Aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel. Take a wife for yourself there, from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.'
28.explanation: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him not to marry a Canaanite woman, but to take a wife from the daughters of Laban in Paddan Aram.

28.question: What did Esau do when he realized how displeasing the Canaanite women were to his father Isaac?
options: He went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had
He built an altar of repentance
28.correctAnswer: He went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had
28.explanation: Esau realized how displeasing the Canaanite women were to his father Isaac; so he went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Ishmael.

28.question: What did Jacob use as a pillow when the sun set near a certain place on his journey to Haran?
options: One of the stones there, which he put under his head as he lay down to sleep
28.correctAnswer: One of the stones there, which he put under his head as he lay down to sleep
28.explanation: Taking one of the stones there, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.

28.question: What did Jacob see in his famous dream in Genesis 28:12?
options: A fleet of golden chariots flying in the clouds
A stairway (ladder) resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it
A river of crystal running through a garden
A mountain engulfed in volcanic fire
28.correctAnswer: A stairway (ladder) resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it
28.explanation: He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

28.question: Who stood above the stairway, and what covenant promise did He declare to Jacob?
options: The Lord, saying: 'I am the Lord, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you are lying... All peoples on earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.'
28.correctAnswer: The Lord, saying: 'I am the Lord, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you are lying... All peoples on earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.'
28.explanation: There above it stood the Lord, confirming the Abrahamic covenant of land, countless descendants like dust, and universal blessing.

28.question: What personal guarantee of divine presence did God give Jacob in Genesis 28:15?
options: 'I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.'
'You will never face conflict with Laban'
28.correctAnswer: 'I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.'
28.explanation: God promised His personal presence: 'I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.'

28.question: What was Jacob's awe-struck declaration when he woke from his sleep?
options: 'Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware of it... How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven.'
'I must hurry before the sun rises'
28.correctAnswer: 'Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware of it... How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven.'
28.explanation: When Jacob awoke from his sleep, he thought, 'Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware of it.' He was afraid and said, 'How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven.'

28.question: What did Jacob do early the next morning with the stone he had used as a pillow?
options: He cast it into a river
He took the stone, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it
He broke it into twelve pieces
He buried it in the earth
28.correctAnswer: He took the stone, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it
28.explanation: Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had placed under his head and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on top of it.

28.question: What name did Jacob give to that place, which had formerly been called Luz?
28.explanation: Genesis 28:19 states: 'He called that place Bethel, though the city used to be called Luz.'

28.question: What vow did Jacob make regarding his devotion and his possessions if God watched over him and brought him back safely?
options: He would never cut his hair
'Then the Lord will be my God and this stone... will be God’s house, and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth (a tithe).'
He would build a golden wall
28.correctAnswer: 'Then the Lord will be my God and this stone... will be God’s house, and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth (a tithe).'
28.explanation: Jacob vowed: 'If God will be with me and will watch over me on this journey... then the Lord will be my God... and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth.'

29.question: What covered the mouth of the well in the open country when Jacob arrived in the land of the eastern peoples?
options: A large stone over the mouth of the well
29.correctAnswer: A large stone over the mouth of the well
29.explanation: A large stone was over the mouth of the well. When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone away.

29.question: Who approached the well with her father's sheep while Jacob was speaking with the shepherds?
options: Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, for she was a shepherdess
29.correctAnswer: Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, for she was a shepherdess
29.explanation: While he was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

29.question: What feat of physical strength and emotion did Jacob perform when he saw his cousin Rachel?
options: He challenged the shepherds to a duel
He went over and rolled the heavy stone away from the mouth of the well, watered his uncle's sheep, kissed Rachel, and wept aloud
29.correctAnswer: He went over and rolled the heavy stone away from the mouth of the well, watered his uncle's sheep, kissed Rachel, and wept aloud
29.explanation: Jacob went over and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle Laban’s sheep. Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to weep aloud.

29.question: How does Genesis 29:16–17 describe the appearance of Laban's two daughters, Leah and Rachel?
options: Leah had weak (delicate) eyes, but Rachel had a lovely figure and was beautiful
Leah was tall and dark; Rachel was short and fair
29.correctAnswer: Leah had weak (delicate) eyes, but Rachel had a lovely figure and was beautiful
29.explanation: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel. Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel had a lovely figure and was beautiful.

29.question: What wages did Jacob propose to Laban in exchange for marrying younger daughter Rachel?
options: To work seven years for his younger daughter Rachel
To build a stone house for Laban
29.correctAnswer: To work seven years for his younger daughter Rachel
29.explanation: Jacob was in love with Rachel and said, 'I’ll work for you seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel.'

29.question: How did the seven years of service feel to Jacob, according to the poetic words of Genesis 29:20?
options: Like an eternity of hard slavery
They seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her
29.correctAnswer: They seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her
29.explanation: Genesis 29:20 beautifully states: 'So Jacob served seven years to get Rachel, but they seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her.'

29.question: What deception did Laban perpetrate on the wedding night in Genesis 29:23–25?
options: In the darkness of evening he brought his older daughter Leah to Jacob, and when morning came, it was Leah!
He gave him no wife at all
29.correctAnswer: In the darkness of evening he brought his older daughter Leah to Jacob, and when morning came, it was Leah!
29.explanation: When evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob... When morning came, there was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, 'What is this you have done to me? I served you for Rachel, didn’t I? Why have you deceived me?'

29.question: What cultural justification did Laban give for switching the brides?
options: 'It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one.'
29.correctAnswer: 'It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one.'
29.explanation: Laban replied, 'It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one.'

29.question: What agreement did Laban offer so Jacob could also marry Rachel?
options: 'Finish this daughter’s bridal week; then we will give you the younger one also, in return for another seven years of work.'
29.correctAnswer: 'Finish this daughter’s bridal week; then we will give you the younger one also, in return for another seven years of work.'
29.explanation: Jacob finished Leah's bridal week; then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife, and Jacob served another seven years. He loved Rachel more than Leah.

29.question: What were the names and birth order of the four sons Leah bore when the Lord saw she was unloved?
options: Reuben ('The Lord has seen my misery'), Simeon ('The Lord heard'), Levi ('attached'), and Judah ('This time I will praise the Lord')
29.correctAnswer: Reuben ('The Lord has seen my misery'), Simeon ('The Lord heard'), Levi ('attached'), and Judah ('This time I will praise the Lord')
29.explanation: Leah bore four sons in sequence: Reuben ('The Lord has seen my misery'), Simeon ('The Lord heard that I am not loved'), Levi ('Now at last my husband will become attached to me'), and Judah ('This time I will praise the Lord').

30.question: What desperate demand did childless Rachel make of Jacob in Genesis 30:1?
30.explanation: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing Jacob any children, she became jealous of her sister and said to Jacob, 'Give me children, or I’ll die!'

30.question: Which two sons were born to Jacob through Rachel's servant Bilhah?
options: Dan ('God has vindicated me') and Naphtali ('I have had a great struggle')
30.correctAnswer: Dan ('God has vindicated me') and Naphtali ('I have had a great struggle')
30.explanation: Bilhah bore Dan ('God has vindicated me') and Naphtali ('I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won').

30.question: Which two sons were born to Jacob through Leah's servant Zilpah?
options: Gad ('What good fortune!') and Asher ('How happy I am!')
30.correctAnswer: Gad ('What good fortune!') and Asher ('How happy I am!')
30.explanation: Zilpah bore Gad ('What good fortune!') and Asher ('How happy I am! The women will call me happy').

30.question: What plant did Reuben find in the fields during the wheat harvest, which Rachel traded with Leah for a night with Jacob?
30.explanation: During wheat harvest, Reuben went out into the fields and found some mandrakes, which he brought to his mother Leah. Rachel asked for them in exchange for Leah spending the night with Jacob.

30.question: Which subsequent children did Leah bear to Jacob in Genesis 30:17–21?
options: Issachar ('God has rewarded me'), Zebulun ('God has presented me with a precious gift'), and a daughter named Dinah
30.correctAnswer: Issachar ('God has rewarded me'), Zebulun ('God has presented me with a precious gift'), and a daughter named Dinah
30.explanation: God listened to Leah and she bore a fifth son named Issachar, a sixth son named Zebulun, and later gave birth to a daughter named Dinah.

30.question: What happened when God remembered Rachel in Genesis 30:22–24?
options: God listened to her and enabled her to conceive; she gave birth to a son and named him Joseph ('May the Lord add to me another son')
30.correctAnswer: God listened to her and enabled her to conceive; she gave birth to a son and named him Joseph ('May the Lord add to me another son')
30.explanation: Then God remembered Rachel; he listened to her and enabled her to conceive. She gave birth to a son and named him Joseph, saying, 'May the Lord add to me another son.'

30.question: What request did Jacob make to Laban after the birth of Joseph?
options: 'Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland... let me take my wives and children, for whom I have served you, and go.'
To become chief over all Haran
30.correctAnswer: 'Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland... let me take my wives and children, for whom I have served you, and go.'
30.explanation: After Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, 'Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland.'

30.question: What wage agreement did Jacob propose regarding the flocks in Genesis 30:31–33?
options: All pure white sheep would be his
Every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat would be his wages
Half of all milk and wool
A fixed salary of 30 shekels per month
30.correctAnswer: Every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat would be his wages
30.explanation: Jacob agreed: 'Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb and every spotted or speckled goat. They will be my wages.'

30.question: What selective breeding method did Jacob employ using peeled branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees?
options: He carved idols into the wood
He peeled white stripes on the branches and placed them in the watering troughs in front of the flocks when the stronger animals were in heat
He burned the branches to create sacred smoke
He boiled the bark in the water
30.correctAnswer: He peeled white stripes on the branches and placed them in the watering troughs in front of the flocks when the stronger animals were in heat
30.explanation: Jacob took fresh-cut branches from poplar, almond, and plane trees and made white stripes on them by peeling the bark, placing them in troughs before the mating flocks.

30.question: How does Genesis 30:43 describe Jacob's material outcome as a result of God's blessing on his work?
options: In this way the man grew exceedingly prosperous and came to own large flocks, and female and male slaves, and camels and donkeys
He lost all his sheep to sickness
He traded his family for land
30.correctAnswer: In this way the man grew exceedingly prosperous and came to own large flocks, and female and male slaves, and camels and donkeys
30.explanation: Genesis 30:43 states: 'In this way the man grew exceedingly prosperous and came to own large flocks, and female and male servants, and camels and donkeys.'

31.question: What complaint from Laban's sons did Jacob hear in Genesis 31:1?
options: 'Jacob has taken everything our father owned and has gained all this wealth from what belonged to our father.'
31.correctAnswer: 'Jacob has taken everything our father owned and has gained all this wealth from what belonged to our father.'
31.explanation: Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, 'Jacob has taken everything our father owned and has gained all this wealth from what belonged to our father.'

31.question: What did the Lord command Jacob in Genesis 31:3?
options: 'Go back to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you.'
31.correctAnswer: 'Go back to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you.'
31.explanation: Then the Lord said to Jacob: 'Go back to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you.'

31.question: How many times did Jacob tell Rachel and Leah that Laban had changed his wages?
31.explanation: Jacob told his wives: 'yet your father has cheated me by changing my wages ten times. However, God has not allowed him to harm me.'

31.question: What did Rachel steal from her father Laban while he was away shearing sheep?
31.explanation: When Laban had gone to shear his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household gods.

31.question: How many days did Laban pursue Jacob before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead?
31.explanation: Laban took his relatives with him and pursued Jacob for seven days and caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

31.question: How did God warn Laban in a dream by night before he confronted Jacob?
options: 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'
31.correctAnswer: 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'
31.explanation: God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and said to him: 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'

31.question: How did Rachel conceal the stolen household gods when Laban searched her tent?
options: She threw them into the well
She put them in her camel’s saddle and sat on them, claiming she could not stand up because of her monthly period
31.correctAnswer: She put them in her camel’s saddle and sat on them, claiming she could not stand up because of her monthly period
31.explanation: Rachel had taken the household gods, put them inside her camel’s saddle and was sitting on them. So he searched through everything in the tent but found nothing.

31.question: How long in total had Jacob faithfully served Laban in Haran according to Genesis 31:38–41?
31.explanation: Jacob rebuked Laban: 'I have been with you for twenty years now... It was like this for the twenty years I was in your household. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks.'

31.question: What monument did Jacob and his relatives pile up as a witness of peace between them?
options: A heap of stones (cairn), which was named Galeed and Mizpah
31.correctAnswer: A heap of stones (cairn), which was named Galeed and Mizpah
31.explanation: Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar, and they gathered stones into a heap. Laban said, 'This heap is a witness between you and me today.' That is why it was called Galeed and Mizpah.

31.question: What famous covenant watch-word is associated with Mizpah in Genesis 31:49?
options: 'May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.'
31.correctAnswer: 'May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.'
31.explanation: It was also called Mizpah, because he said: 'May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.'

32.question: Who met Jacob on his way after parting from Laban, prompting him to name the place Mahanaim ('two camps')?
32.explanation: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him. When Jacob saw them, he said, 'This is the camp of God!' So he named that place Mahanaim.

32.question: What alarming news did the messengers bring back regarding Esau in Genesis 32:6?
options: Esau was coming to meet him, and four hundred men were with him
32.correctAnswer: Esau was coming to meet him, and four hundred men were with him
32.explanation: The messengers returned saying: 'We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.'

32.question: What protective measure did Jacob take in his great fear and distress in Genesis 32:7–8?
options: He divided the people with him and the flocks and herds into two groups, thinking if Esau attacks one, the other can escape
He hid in a cave alone
32.correctAnswer: He divided the people with him and the flocks and herds into two groups, thinking if Esau attacks one, the other can escape
32.explanation: In great fear and distress Jacob divided the people who were with him into two groups, thinking: 'If Esau comes and attacks one group, the group that is left may escape.'

32.question: What humble confession did Jacob pray to God in Genesis 32:10?
options: 'I have earned all my blessings by my wisdom'
'I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two camps.'
'My brother has no right to be angry'
32.correctAnswer: 'I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two camps.'
32.explanation: Jacob prayed: 'I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two camps.'

32.question: What generous gift did Jacob select from his possessions to appease his brother Esau?
options: Over 550 animals: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams, 30 female camels with colts, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys
One hundred camels loaded with wheat
32.correctAnswer: Over 550 animals: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams, 30 female camels with colts, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys
32.explanation: Jacob selected hundreds of animals arranged in separate droves with space between them as a lavish gift to pacify Esau.

32.question: Which stream or river ford did Jacob send his family and possessions across during the night?
32.explanation: That night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two female servants and his eleven sons and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

32.question: What extraordinary event happened when Jacob was left alone on the riverbank in Genesis 32:24?
options: A man wrestled with him till daybreak
He fell into a deep trance without waking
32.correctAnswer: A man wrestled with him till daybreak
32.explanation: Genesis 32:24 records: 'So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak.'

32.question: What physical injury did the mysterious wrestler inflict on Jacob when He saw He could not overpower him?
options: He touched the socket of Jacob’s hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled
32.correctAnswer: He touched the socket of Jacob’s hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled
32.explanation: When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the socket of Jacob’s hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled with him.

32.question: What new name was given to Jacob, and what was its profound meaning in Genesis 32:28?
options: Israel ('he struggles with God'), because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome
32.correctAnswer: Israel ('he struggles with God'), because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome
32.explanation: Then the man said: 'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.'

32.question: What did Jacob name the place where he wrestled, and why?
options: Peniel ('Face of God'), saying: 'It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.'
32.correctAnswer: Peniel ('Face of God'), saying: 'It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.'
32.explanation: So Jacob called the place Peniel, saying, 'It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.' The sun rose above him as he passed Peniel, limping because of his hip.

33.question: In what order did Jacob arrange his family as he went out to meet Esau and his 400 men?
options: Rachel and Joseph first, then Leah, then the maidservants
The female servants and their children first, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear
All the children together in the front
He kept his family behind a stone wall
33.correctAnswer: The female servants and their children first, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear
33.explanation: He put the female servants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear (protecting his most beloved).

33.question: How many times did Jacob bow down to the ground as he approached his brother Esau?
33.explanation: Genesis 33:3 states: 'He himself went on ahead and bowed down to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.'

33.question: How did Esau unexpectedly react upon reaching Jacob in Genesis 33:4?
options: He raised his sword in anger
Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.
He turned his back and walked away
33.correctAnswer: Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.
33.explanation: Genesis 33:4 records: 'But Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.'

33.question: What did Esau say when he first saw the herds of animals sent as a gift in Genesis 33:9?
options: 'I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.'
33.correctAnswer: 'I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.'
33.explanation: Esau said, 'I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.'

33.question: What extraordinary statement of reconciliation did Jacob speak to Esau in Genesis 33:10?
options: 'To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably.'
'We must never see each other again'
33.correctAnswer: 'To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably.'
33.explanation: Jacob insisted: 'If I have found favor in your eyes, accept this gift from me. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably.'

33.question: Why did Jacob urge Esau to go on ahead without traveling together as one large company?
options: Because he planned to escape by night
Because the children were tender and the nursing flocks would die if driven hard for even one day
33.correctAnswer: Because the children were tender and the nursing flocks would die if driven hard for even one day
33.explanation: Jacob explained: 'My lord knows that the children are tender and that I must care for the ewes and cows that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard just one day, all the animals will die.'

33.question: To which region did Esau return on that day in Genesis 33:16?
33.explanation: Genesis 33:16 notes: 'So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir.'

33.question: Where did Jacob travel next, building a house for himself and shelters (booths) for his livestock?
33.explanation: Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a place for himself and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Succoth.

33.question: From whom did Jacob buy a plot of ground for a hundred pieces of silver near the city of Shechem?
options: From the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem
33.correctAnswer: From the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem
33.explanation: For a hundred pieces of silver, he bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, the plot of ground where he pitched his tent.

33.question: What name did Jacob give to the altar he set up there in Genesis 33:20?
options: El Elohe Israel ('God, the God of Israel')
33.correctAnswer: El Elohe Israel ('God, the God of Israel')
33.explanation: There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel ('God, the God of Israel').

34.question: Who was Dinah in Genesis 34:1?
options: The daughter Leah had borne to Jacob
34.correctAnswer: The daughter Leah had borne to Jacob
34.explanation: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.

34.question: What violation did Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, commit against Dinah?
options: He took her, violated (defiled) her, and shamed her
He drove her out of the city
He forced her to tend sheep
34.correctAnswer: He took her, violated (defiled) her, and shamed her
34.explanation: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of that area, saw her, he took her and violated her.

34.question: How did Shechem feel toward Dinah after the act in Genesis 34:3?
options: His heart was drawn to Dinah; he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her, asking his father to get her as his wife
He sent her away in disgrace
34.correctAnswer: His heart was drawn to Dinah; he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her, asking his father to get her as his wife
34.explanation: His heart was drawn to Dinah daughter of Jacob; he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her, saying to his father Hamor, 'Get me this girl as my wife.'

34.question: How did Jacob's sons react when they came in from the fields and heard what had happened?
options: They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob’s daughter
34.correctAnswer: They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob’s daughter
34.explanation: Jacob’s sons came in from the fields as soon as they heard. They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel; a thing that should not be done.

34.question: What condition did Jacob's sons deceitfully propose before they would agree to intermarriage with the men of Shechem?
options: Every male among them must be circumcised, like Jacob's family
They must surrender all their weapons
They must pay 10,000 shekels of gold
34.correctAnswer: Every male among them must be circumcised, like Jacob's family
34.explanation: They told them: 'We can’t do such a thing; we can’t give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. We will enter into an agreement with you on one condition only: that you become like us by circumcising all your males.'

34.question: Why did Hamor and Shechem persuade the men at the city gate to accept circumcision?
options: Because Shechem loved Dinah, and they argued that Jacob's wealth, livestock, and property would become theirs through intermarriage
34.correctAnswer: Because Shechem loved Dinah, and they argued that Jacob's wealth, livestock, and property would become theirs through intermarriage
34.explanation: Hamor and Shechem argued: 'Won’t their livestock, their property and all their other animals become ours? So let us agree to their terms, and they will settle among us.'

34.question: Which two sons of Jacob took their swords, attacked the unsuspecting city on the third day when all the men were in pain, and killed every male?
options: Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s full brothers
34.correctAnswer: Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s full brothers
34.explanation: Three days later, while all of them were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, took their swords and attacked the unsuspecting city, killing every male.

34.question: What did Simeon and Levi do to Hamor and his son Shechem, and what did they rescue?
options: They killed Hamor and Shechem with the sword, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and left
34.correctAnswer: They killed Hamor and Shechem with the sword, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and left
34.explanation: They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword and took Dinah from Shechem’s house and left.

34.question: What rebuke did Jacob deliver to Simeon and Levi in Genesis 34:30?
options: 'You have brought trouble on me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites... they will band together and destroy me and my household.'
'Why did you leave the sheep behind?'
34.correctAnswer: 'You have brought trouble on me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites... they will band together and destroy me and my household.'
34.explanation: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, 'You have brought trouble on me by making me obnoxious to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people living in this land. We are few in number, and if they join forces against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.'

34.question: What defiant question did Simeon and Levi reply with to justify their violent revenge?
options: 'Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?'
34.correctAnswer: 'Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?'
34.explanation: Genesis 34:31 concludes with their defiant response: 'But they replied, Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?'

35.question: What did God command Jacob to do at the start of Genesis 35?
options: 'Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.'
35.correctAnswer: 'Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.'
35.explanation: God said to Jacob, 'Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.'

35.question: What three commands did Jacob give his household before journeying to Bethel?
options: Sharpen your swords, harness horses, and prepare rations
Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, purify yourselves, and change your clothes
Fast for forty days and remain silent
Sell all the cattle to merchants
35.correctAnswer: Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, purify yourselves, and change your clothes
35.explanation: Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, 'Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.'

35.question: Where did Jacob bury all the foreign gods and the rings in their ears in Genesis 35:4?
35.explanation: They gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the oak at Shechem.

35.question: Why did the surrounding towns not pursue Jacob's family as they set out in Genesis 35:5?
options: The terror of God fell on the towns all around them, so that no one pursued them
The towns were celebrating a festival
Jacob had left behind armed guards
35.correctAnswer: The terror of God fell on the towns all around them, so that no one pursued them
35.explanation: Genesis 35:5 states: 'Then they set out, and the terror of God fell on the towns all around them, so that no one pursued them.'

35.question: Who died at Bethel and was buried under the oak below Bethel, which was named Allon Bakuth ('Oak of Weeping')?
35.explanation: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak outside Bethel. So it was named Allon Bakuth ('Oak of Weeping').

35.question: What name did God reaffirm to Jacob at Bethel, and how did He reveal His own name?
options: 'Your name will no longer be Jacob; your name will be Israel.' And God said, 'I am God Almighty (El Shaddai): be fruitful and increase in number.'
'Your name is Solomon; I am the Lord of hosts'
'Your name is Judah; I am the God of Hebron'
'Your name is Abraham; I am the Rock'
35.correctAnswer: 'Your name will no longer be Jacob; your name will be Israel.' And God said, 'I am God Almighty (El Shaddai): be fruitful and increase in number.'
35.explanation: God said to him, 'Your name is Jacob, but you will no longer be called Jacob; your name will be Israel.' And God said, 'I am God Almighty; be fruitful and increase in number.'

35.question: Where did Rachel experience severe labor and die while giving birth to her second son?
options: Along the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)
35.correctAnswer: Along the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)
35.explanation: While they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth and had great difficulty... So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

35.question: What name did dying Rachel give to the newborn child, and to what did his father Jacob change it?
options: Rachel named him Joseph; Jacob named him Ephraim
Rachel named him Ben-Oni ('son of my trouble/sorrow'), but his father named him Benjamin ('son of my right hand')
Rachel named him Judah; Jacob named him Levi
Rachel named him Moses; Jacob named him Aaron
35.correctAnswer: Rachel named him Ben-Oni ('son of my trouble/sorrow'), but his father named him Benjamin ('son of my right hand')
35.explanation: As she breathed her last—for she was dying—she named her son Ben-Oni. But his father named him Benjamin.

35.question: What grievous sin did Reuben, Jacob's firstborn son, commit in Genesis 35:22?
options: He went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard of it
He attacked the Philistines without permission
35.correctAnswer: He went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard of it
35.explanation: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard of it (costing Reuben his firstborn rights).

35.question: How old was Isaac when he died at Mamre in Hebron, and who buried him?
options: 120 years old; buried by Jacob alone
180 years old; buried by his sons Esau and Jacob
175 years old; buried by Ishmael and Jacob
200 years old; buried by the Hittites
35.correctAnswer: 180 years old; buried by his sons Esau and Jacob
35.explanation: Isaac lived 180 years. Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

36.question: Which nation is descended from Esau according to Genesis 36:1?
36.explanation: Genesis 36:1 opens: 'This is the account of the family line of Esau (that is, Edom).'

36.question: Why did Esau take his wives, sons, daughters, and all his livestock and move away from his brother Jacob?
options: Their possessions were too great for them to remain together; the land where they were staying could not support them both because of their livestock
The king of Canaan drove Esau away
God commanded Esau to live in Egypt
36.correctAnswer: Their possessions were too great for them to remain together; the land where they were staying could not support them both because of their livestock
36.explanation: Their possessions were too great for them to remain together; the land where they were staying could not support them both because of their livestock.

36.question: In which mountainous hill country did Esau (Edom) settle?
36.explanation: So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the hill country of Seir.

36.question: Who was Esau's firstborn son born to his wife Adah?
36.explanation: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath bore Reuel, and Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

36.question: Which infamous tribe descended from Timna, the concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz?
36.explanation: Eliphaz’s concubine Timna bore him Amalek. These were grandsons of Esau’s wife Adah.

36.question: Who were the native inhabitants of the hill country of Seir before Esau's descendants assimilated with them?
options: The sons of Seir the Horite
36.correctAnswer: The sons of Seir the Horite
36.explanation: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the region: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan.

36.question: What notable discovery did Anah make while pasturing his father Zibeon's donkeys in the desert in Genesis 36:24?
options: He discovered hot springs in the desert
A hidden oasis with wild figs
36.correctAnswer: He discovered hot springs in the desert
36.explanation: Genesis 36:24 records: 'This is the Anah who discovered the hot springs in the desert while he was grazing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.'

36.question: What historical note is attached to the list of Edomite kings in Genesis 36:31?
options: 'These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned.'
36.correctAnswer: 'These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned.'
36.explanation: Genesis 36:31 states: 'These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned.'

36.question: Who was the first king named who reigned in Edom, whose city was Dinhabah?
options: Husham from the land of the Temanites
36.explanation: Bela son of Beor became king of Edom. His city was named Dinhabah.

36.question: What title was given to the tribal clan leaders of Esau listed in Genesis 36:40–43?
36.explanation: These were the chiefs descended from Esau, by name, according to their clans and regions: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel and Iram.

37.question: How old was Joseph when he tended the flocks with his half-brothers, the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah?
37.explanation: Joseph, a young man of seventeen, was tending the flocks with his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives.

37.question: Why did Israel (Jacob) love Joseph more than any of his other sons?
options: Because he was a mighty hunter
Because he had been born to him in his old age
37.correctAnswer: Because he had been born to him in his old age
37.explanation: Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, because he had been born to him in his old age; and he made an ornate robe (coat of many colors) for him.

37.question: How did Joseph's brothers react when they saw that their father loved him more than all of them?
options: They hated him and could not speak a kind word to him
37.correctAnswer: They hated him and could not speak a kind word to him
37.explanation: When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.

37.question: What occurred in Joseph's first prophetic dream in Genesis 37:7?
options: Seven lean cows ate seven fat cows
We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it
A ladder reached up to heaven
37.correctAnswer: We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it
37.explanation: Joseph dreamed: 'We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it.'

37.question: What celestial bodies bowed down to Joseph in his second dream in Genesis 37:9?
options: The sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me
37.correctAnswer: The sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me
37.explanation: He had another dream: 'Listen,' he said, 'I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.'

37.question: Where did Joseph find his brothers after being sent by Jacob from the Valley of Hebron via Shechem?
37.explanation: A man told him, 'They have moved on from here. I heard them say, Let’s go to Dothan.' So Joseph went after his brothers and found them near Dothan.

37.question: What did the brothers say when they saw Joseph approaching in the distance?
options: 'Here comes that dreamer! Come now, let’s kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns... Then we’ll see what comes of his dreams.'
37.correctAnswer: 'Here comes that dreamer! Come now, let’s kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns... Then we’ll see what comes of his dreams.'
37.explanation: They plotted: 'Here comes that dreamer! Come now, let’s kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns and say that a ferocious animal devoured him. Then we’ll see what comes of his dreams.'

37.question: Who intervened to save Joseph's life, intending to rescue him later and take him back to his father?
options: Reuben ('Don’t shed any blood. Throw him into this cistern here in the wilderness, but don’t lay a hand on him.')
37.correctAnswer: Reuben ('Don’t shed any blood. Throw him into this cistern here in the wilderness, but don’t lay a hand on him.')
37.explanation: When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue him from their hands. 'Let’s not take his life,' he said. Reuben said this to rescue him from them and take him back to his father.

37.question: What did Judah propose when they saw an Ishmaelite caravan coming from Gilead on their way to Egypt?
options: 'What will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood? Come, let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay our hands on him; after all, he is our brother.'
37.correctAnswer: 'What will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood? Come, let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay our hands on him; after all, he is our brother.'
37.explanation: Judah proposed selling Joseph rather than leaving him to die. So they pulled Joseph out of the cistern and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites.

37.question: How did the brothers deceive their father Jacob, and to whom was Joseph sold in Egypt?
options: They said Joseph drowned; sold to a merchant in Tyre

They dipped Joseph’s ornate robe in goat's blood, showing it to Jacob who mourned bitterly ('a ferocious animal has devoured him'); Joseph was sold in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the captain of the guard
They said Joseph was stolen by robbers; sold to a farmer in Goshen
37.correctAnswer: They dipped Joseph’s ornate robe in goat's blood, showing it to Jacob who mourned bitterly ('a ferocious animal has devoured him'); Joseph was sold in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the captain of the guard
37.explanation: They slaughtered a goat and dipped the robe in blood, bringing it to Jacob who tore his clothes and wept for his son. Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard.

38.question: With which Adullamite man did Judah stay after leaving his brothers?
38.explanation: At that time, Judah left his brothers and went down to stay with a man of Adullam named Hirah.

38.question: Who were the three sons born to Judah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanite?
38.explanation: She conceived and gave birth to a son, whom he named Er. She conceived again and gave birth to Onan, and yet another son named Shelah.

38.question: Who was the woman Judah chose as a wife for his firstborn son Er?
38.explanation: Judah got a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

38.question: What happened to Er in Genesis 38:7?
options: Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the Lord’s sight; so the Lord put him to death
38.correctAnswer: Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the Lord’s sight; so the Lord put him to death
38.explanation: Genesis 38:7 states: 'But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the Lord’s sight; so the Lord put him to death.'

38.question: What duty did Judah assign to Onan under the ancient levirate custom, and why did the Lord put Onan to death?
options: To build a house; he refused to work
