To sleep with his brother’s wife and fulfill his duty as brother-in-law to produce offspring for his brother; Onan spilled his semen on the ground, which was wicked in the Lord’s sight
To sacrifice an ox; he offered an unclean goat
To pay a fine to Tamar
38.correctAnswer: To sleep with his brother’s wife and fulfill his duty as brother-in-law to produce offspring for his brother; Onan spilled his semen on the ground, which was wicked in the Lord’s sight
38.explanation: Onan knew that the child would not be his, so whenever he slept with his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground to keep from providing offspring for his brother. What he did was wicked in the Lord’s sight; so the Lord put him to death also.

38.question: What promise did Judah make to Tamar, but failed to fulfill as Shelah grew up?
options: To live as a widow in her father’s household until his youngest son Shelah grew up, but he feared Shelah would die like his brothers
To send her back to Egypt
38.correctAnswer: To live as a widow in her father’s household until his youngest son Shelah grew up, but he feared Shelah would die like his brothers
38.explanation: Judah told Tamar to wait as a widow until Shelah was grown, but he neglected to give her to Shelah when he grew up, fearing Shelah might also die.

38.question: How did Tamar disguise herself when she heard Judah was going up to Timnah to shear his sheep?
options: She took off her widow’s clothes, covered herself with a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim on the road to Timnah
38.correctAnswer: She took off her widow’s clothes, covered herself with a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim on the road to Timnah
38.explanation: She took off her widow's clothes, covered herself with a veil to disguise herself, and sat by the road, because she saw that Shelah had grown up and yet she had not been given to him as his wife.

38.question: What three personal items did Tamar demand from Judah as a pledge until he sent a young goat from his flock?
options: His seal and its cord, and the staff in his hand
38.correctAnswer: His seal and its cord, and the staff in his hand
38.explanation: He asked, 'What pledge should I give you?' 'Your seal and its cord, and the staff in your hand,' she answered. So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.

38.question: What confession did Judah utter when Tamar produced the seal, cord, and staff as she was being brought out to be burned?
options: 'She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn’t give her to my son Shelah.'
'The items were stolen from my tent'
38.correctAnswer: 'She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn’t give her to my son Shelah.'
38.explanation: Judah recognized them and said: 'She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn’t give her to my son Shelah.' And he did not sleep with her again.

38.question: Who were the twin sons born to Tamar, one of whom entered the direct messianic lineage of David and Jesus?
options: Perez ('breaking out') and Zerah (around whose wrist a scarlet thread was tied)
38.correctAnswer: Perez ('breaking out') and Zerah (around whose wrist a scarlet thread was tied)
38.explanation: Perez broke out first, followed by his twin brother Zerah with the scarlet thread. Perez became the ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

39.question: Who bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites in Egypt in Genesis 39:1?
options: Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard
An Egyptian merchant at the port
39.correctAnswer: Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard
39.explanation: Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.

39.question: What foundational truth is repeated in Genesis 39:2 regarding Joseph's success?
options: Joseph was skilled in martial arts
The Lord was with Joseph so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master
Potiphar was a relative of Abraham
39.correctAnswer: The Lord was with Joseph so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master
39.explanation: Genesis 39:2 states: 'The Lord was with Joseph so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master.'

39.question: What position of responsibility did Potiphar bestow upon Joseph?
options: He made him attendant and put him in charge of his household, entrusting to his care everything he owned
39.correctAnswer: He made him attendant and put him in charge of his household, entrusting to his care everything he owned
39.explanation: Joseph found favor in his eyes and became his attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household, and he entrusted to his care everything he owned.

39.question: How does Genesis 39:6 describe Joseph's physical appearance?
options: Now Joseph was well-built and handsome
39.correctAnswer: Now Joseph was well-built and handsome
39.explanation: Genesis 39:6 records: 'Now Joseph was well-built and handsome.'

39.question: What persistent temptation did Potiphar's wife place before Joseph day after day?
options: She took notice of Joseph and said, 'Come to bed with me!'
39.correctAnswer: She took notice of Joseph and said, 'Come to bed with me!'
39.explanation: His master’s wife took notice of Joseph and said, 'Come to bed with me!' But he refused, day after day.

39.question: What moral and theological reason did Joseph proclaim for refusing her solicitation in Genesis 39:9?
options: 'How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?'
39.correctAnswer: 'How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?'
39.explanation: Joseph declared: 'My master has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?'

39.question: What happened on the day Joseph went into the house to do his duties and none of the household servants was inside?
options: She locked him in a vault
She caught him by his cloak and said, 'Come to bed with me!' But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house
39.correctAnswer: She caught him by his cloak and said, 'Come to bed with me!' But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house
39.explanation: She caught him by his cloak and said, 'Come to bed with me!' But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house.

39.question: How did Potiphar's wife falsely accuse Joseph when her husband came home?
options: She claimed Joseph had stolen money
She held his cloak and claimed: 'That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me, but when I screamed, he left his cloak and ran outside.'
She claimed Joseph broke the furniture
She said Joseph was an escaped prisoner
39.correctAnswer: She held his cloak and claimed: 'That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me, but when I screamed, he left his cloak and ran outside.'
39.explanation: She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home, and told him the false accusation, stoking Potiphar's wrath.

39.question: Where did Potiphar put Joseph in his burning anger?
options: He took him and put him in prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined
He sent him to work in the stone quarries
39.correctAnswer: He took him and put him in prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined
39.explanation: Joseph’s master took him and put him in prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined.

39.question: What comfort and providence accompanied Joseph inside the prison in Genesis 39:21–23?
options: The Lord was with him; He showed him kindness and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden, who put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners
39.correctAnswer: The Lord was with him; He showed him kindness and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden, who put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners
39.explanation: The Lord was with him; he showed him kindness and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden. The warden paid no attention to anything under Joseph’s care, because the Lord was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.

40.question: Which two royal Egyptian officials offended Pharaoh and were put in custody in the prison where Joseph was confined?
options: The chief scribe and the chief general
The chief cupbearer and the chief baker
40.correctAnswer: The chief cupbearer and the chief baker
40.explanation: Some time later, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their master. Pharaoh was angry with his two officials and put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was confined.

40.question: What happened to both the cupbearer and the baker on the same night in Genesis 40:5?
options: Each of the two men had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own
They received a letter from Pharaoh
40.correctAnswer: Each of the two men had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own
40.explanation: Each of the two men—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were being held in prison—had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own.

40.question: What did Joseph notice and ask when he visited them the next morning?
options: He noticed they had not eaten
He saw that they were dejected and asked, 'Why are your faces so sad today?'
He asked if they had finished their work
He warned them of an inspection
40.correctAnswer: He saw that they were dejected and asked, 'Why are your faces so sad today?'
40.explanation: When Joseph came to them the next morning, he saw that they were dejected. So he asked Pharaoh’s officials who were in custody with him, 'Why are your faces so sad today?'

40.question: What memorable theological reply did Joseph give when they complained, 'We both had dreams, and there is no one to interpret them'?
options: 'I am the wisest man in Egypt'
'Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.'
'Pay me silver and I will tell you'
40.correctAnswer: 'Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.'
40.explanation: Then Joseph said to them: 'Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.'

40.question: What did the chief cupbearer see in his dream in Genesis 40:9–11?
options: Seven loaves of bread in a basket
A vine with three branches; it budded, blossomed, and produced clusters of ripe grapes, which he squeezed into Pharaoh's cup and placed in Pharaoh's hand
A golden river flowing through the palace
40.correctAnswer: A vine with three branches; it budded, blossomed, and produced clusters of ripe grapes, which he squeezed into Pharaoh's cup and placed in Pharaoh's hand
40.explanation: In his dream, he saw a vine with three branches that produced ripe grapes; Pharaoh's cup was in his hand, and he squeezed the grapes into Pharaoh's cup and placed it in Pharaoh's hand.

40.question: What was the interpretation of the cupbearer's dream given by Joseph?
options: The three branches are three years in prison
The three branches are three days; within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position as cupbearer
He will be exiled to Canaan
He will be made governor of Memphis
40.correctAnswer: The three branches are three days; within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position as cupbearer
40.explanation: Joseph said: 'The three branches are three days. Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you used to do.'

40.question: What personal favor did Joseph ask of the cupbearer in Genesis 40:14–15?
options: 'When all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison... for I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.'
To bring him food from the palace
40.correctAnswer: 'When all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison... for I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.'
40.explanation: Joseph pleaded: 'When all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison. I was forcibly carried off from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.'

40.question: What did the chief baker see in his dream in Genesis 40:16–17?
options: Three baskets of bread on his head; in the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket
40.correctAnswer: Three baskets of bread on his head; in the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket
40.explanation: There were three baskets of bread on his head. In the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on his head.

40.question: What grim interpretation did Joseph give to the chief baker's dream in Genesis 40:18–19?
options: He would be pardoned after three months
The three baskets are three days; within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and impale your body on a pole, and the birds will eat away your flesh
He would be demoted to a servant
He would be exiled to the desert
40.correctAnswer: The three baskets are three days; within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and impale your body on a pole, and the birds will eat away your flesh
40.explanation: Joseph said: 'The three baskets are three days. Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and impale your body on a pole. And the birds will eat away your flesh.'

40.question: What happened on the third day (Pharaoh's birthday), and what did the chief cupbearer do regarding Joseph?
options: Both were pardoned; cupbearer rewarded Joseph
Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, but he impaled the chief baker just as Joseph had said; yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him
40.correctAnswer: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, but he impaled the chief baker just as Joseph had said; yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him
40.explanation: Now the third day was Pharaoh’s birthday. He restored the chief cupbearer to his position, but he impaled the chief baker, just as Joseph had said. 'The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.'

41.question: How much time passed before Pharaoh had his dreams while Joseph remained forgotten in prison?
41.explanation: Genesis 41:1 opens: 'When two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing by the Nile.'

41.question: What two dreams did Pharaoh have in Genesis 41:1–7?
options: Seven eagles fighting seven lions, followed by a storm
Seven sleek, fat cows eaten by seven ugly, gaunt cows; then seven plump, good heads of grain swallowed by seven thin, scorched heads of grain
A golden pyramid collapsing into the sea
The sun falling from the sky
41.correctAnswer: Seven sleek, fat cows eaten by seven ugly, gaunt cows; then seven plump, good heads of grain swallowed by seven thin, scorched heads of grain
41.explanation: Seven sleek and fat cows were eaten by seven ugly and gaunt cows. Then seven plump heads of grain were swallowed up by seven thin heads scorched by the east wind.

41.question: What prompted the chief cupbearer to finally remember Joseph in Genesis 41:9–13?
options: When none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret Pharaoh's dreams, the cupbearer remembered the young Hebrew who had interpreted his dream in prison
Pharaoh offered a reward of gold
41.correctAnswer: When none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret Pharaoh's dreams, the cupbearer remembered the young Hebrew who had interpreted his dream in prison
41.explanation: When Pharaoh was troubled and none of Egypt's wise men could interpret his dreams, the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, 'Today I am reminded of my shortcomings... There was a young Hebrew with us in prison.'

41.question: What did Joseph say when Pharaoh told him, 'I have heard that when you hear a dream you can interpret it'?
options: 'I am indeed the greatest interpreter in the world'
'I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.'
'Pay me a thousand talents of silver first'
'I need three days to study the stars'
41.correctAnswer: 'I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.'
41.explanation: Joseph answered Pharaoh with humility: 'I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.'

41.question: What was the interpretation of the seven cows and seven heads of grain given by Joseph?
options: Seven years of military victories followed by seven years of plague
Seven years of great abundance throughout the land of Egypt, followed by seven years of severe famine that will ravage the land
The building of fourteen new store cities
41.correctAnswer: Seven years of great abundance throughout the land of Egypt, followed by seven years of severe famine that will ravage the land
41.explanation: Joseph explained: 'Seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt, but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will ravage the land.'

41.question: Why was the dream given to Pharaoh in two different forms according to Genesis 41:32?
options: Because Pharaoh had forgotten the first dream
Because the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon
Because Egypt had two kingdoms (Upper and Lower)
Because of two different harvest seasons
41.correctAnswer: Because the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon
41.explanation: The reason the dream was given to Pharaoh in two forms is that the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon.

41.question: What administrative plan did Joseph recommend to Pharaoh to prepare for the coming famine?
options: To conquer neighboring lands for grain
To appoint a discerning and wise man over Egypt, appoint commissioners to collect a fifth (20%) of the harvest during the seven years of abundance, and store the grain under Pharaoh's guard
To slaughter all the cattle immediately
To build higher irrigation canals on the Nile
41.correctAnswer: To appoint a discerning and wise man over Egypt, appoint commissioners to collect a fifth (20%) of the harvest during the seven years of abundance, and store the grain under Pharaoh's guard
41.explanation: Joseph advised: 'Let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man and put him in charge of the land of Egypt. Let them gather all the food of these good years... stored up for the country to be used during the seven years of famine.'

41.question: What did Pharaoh say to his officials in Genesis 41:38 before promoting Joseph?
options: 'Can we find anyone like this man, one in whom is the spirit of God?'
'Let us test him for another year'
41.correctAnswer: 'Can we find anyone like this man, one in whom is the spirit of God?'
41.explanation: So Pharaoh asked them: 'Can we find anyone like this man, one in whom is the spirit of God?'

41.question: What royal honors and position did Pharaoh bestow upon Joseph in Genesis 41:41–45?
options: Second-in-command over all Egypt, putting his signet ring on his finger, dressed in fine linen with a gold chain, riding in the chariot as his second-in-command, and given the name Zaphenath-Paneah
41.correctAnswer: Second-in-command over all Egypt, putting his signet ring on his finger, dressed in fine linen with a gold chain, riding in the chariot as his second-in-command, and given the name Zaphenath-Paneah
41.explanation: Pharaoh said: 'I hereby put you in charge of the whole land of Egypt.' He took his signet ring and put it on Joseph's finger, dressed him in fine linen, placed a gold chain around his neck, had him ride in his second chariot, and gave him the name Zaphenath-Paneah.

41.question: How old was Joseph when he entered the service of Pharaoh, and what were the names of his two sons born before the famine?
options: 30 years old; Manasseh ('God has made me forget all my trouble') and Ephraim ('God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering')
41.correctAnswer: 30 years old; Manasseh ('God has made me forget all my trouble') and Ephraim ('God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering')
41.explanation: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh. Before the years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph: Manasseh and Ephraim.

42.question: Why did Jacob send ten of his sons down to Egypt in Genesis 42:1–3?
options: To seek an alliance with Pharaoh
Because there was grain in Egypt while famine raged in Canaan, so they could buy food and live and not die
42.correctAnswer: Because there was grain in Egypt while famine raged in Canaan, so they could buy food and live and not die
42.explanation: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons: 'Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.'

42.question: Which son did Jacob refuse to send with his brothers to Egypt, and why?
options: Judah, because he was his counselor
Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, because Jacob was afraid that harm might come to him
Reuben, because he was the firstborn
42.correctAnswer: Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, because Jacob was afraid that harm might come to him
42.explanation: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with the others, because he was afraid that harm might come to him.

42.question: What did Joseph's brothers do when they arrived before Joseph in Genesis 42:6, fulfilling his teenage dreams?
options: They bowed down to him with their faces to the ground
They recognized him immediately and wept
They offered him gifts of camels
42.correctAnswer: They bowed down to him with their faces to the ground
42.explanation: Now Joseph was the governor of the land, the person who sold grain to all its people. So when Joseph’s brothers arrived, they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

42.question: How did Joseph treat his brothers when he recognized them, while they did not recognize him?
options: He pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them, accusing them: 'You are spies! You have come to see where our land is unprotected.'
He revealed himself at once with joy
He gave them all the grain for free
42.correctAnswer: He pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them, accusing them: 'You are spies! You have come to see where our land is unprotected.'
42.explanation: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, he pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them. 'You are spies!' he said to them. 'You have come to see where our land is unprotected.'

42.question: How did the brothers explain their family background to Joseph in Genesis 42:13?
options: 'Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man, who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.'
42.correctAnswer: 'Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man, who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.'
42.explanation: They replied: 'Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man, who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.'

42.question: What test did Joseph establish on the third day to verify that they were honest men and not spies?
options: They had to build a storehouse in Egypt
One brother would be kept confined in prison while the others took grain back to their starving households and brought their youngest brother back to Egypt
They had to fight an Egyptian champion
They had to swear an oath to Pharaoh's gods
42.correctAnswer: One brother would be kept confined in prison while the others took grain back to their starving households and brought their youngest brother back to Egypt
42.explanation: On the third day, Joseph said to them: 'Do this and you will live, for I fear God: If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay here in prison, while the rest of you go and take grain back... But you must bring your youngest brother to me.'

42.question: What did the brothers say among themselves, unaware that Joseph understood them because an interpreter was being used?
options: 'Let us plan an attack on Egypt'
'Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw how distressed he was when he pleaded with us for his life, but we would not listen; that’s why this distress has come on us.'
42.correctAnswer: 'Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw how distressed he was when he pleaded with us for his life, but we would not listen; that’s why this distress has come on us.'
42.explanation: They confessed their guilt over Joseph: 'Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw how distressed he was when he pleaded with us for his life, but we would not listen; that’s why this distress has come on us.'

42.question: Which brother was bound before their eyes to remain in prison while the others returned to Canaan?
42.explanation: Joseph turned away from them and began to weep, but then came back and spoke to them again. He had Simeon taken from them and bound before their eyes.

42.question: What shocking discovery did one of the brothers make at the lodging place when opening his sack to feed his donkey?
options: His silver had been returned into the mouth of his sack
42.correctAnswer: His silver had been returned into the mouth of his sack
42.explanation: At the place where they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of his sack. Their hearts sank and they turned to each other trembling and said, 'What is this that God has done to us?'

42.question: What anguished cry did Jacob make when his sons reported everything in Genesis 42:36?
options: 'You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!'
'I will go down to Egypt myself'
42.correctAnswer: 'You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!'
42.explanation: Their father Jacob said to them: 'You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!'

43.question: What condition did Judah remind Jacob of when Jacob told them to go buy a little more food?
options: 'The man solemnly warned us, You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'
43.correctAnswer: 'The man solemnly warned us, You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'
43.explanation: Judah said to him: 'The man solemnly warned us, You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you. If you will send our brother along with us, we will go down and buy food for you.'

43.question: What personal guarantee did Judah give to Jacob to secure Benjamin's release for the journey?
options: He offered his own children as slaves
'I myself will guarantee his safety; you can hold me personally responsible for him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him here before you, I will bear the blame before you all my life.'
He gave Jacob all his cattle
He signed a deed in Hebron
43.correctAnswer: 'I myself will guarantee his safety; you can hold me personally responsible for him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him here before you, I will bear the blame before you all my life.'
43.explanation: Judah pledged personal surety: 'I myself will guarantee his safety; you can hold me personally responsible for him. If I do not bring him back to you... I will bear the blame before you all my life.'

43.question: What gifts from the best products of the land did Israel instruct his sons to take down to the ruler of Egypt?
options: A little balm and a little honey, some spices and myrrh, some pistachio nuts and almonds, along with double the silver
43.correctAnswer: A little balm and a little honey, some spices and myrrh, some pistachio nuts and almonds, along with double the silver

49.explanation: Then Jacob called for his sons and said: 'Gather around so I can tell you what will happen to you in days to come.'

49.question: Why did Reuben lose his preeminence as the firstborn in Jacob's blessing in Genesis 49:3–4?
options: Because he was 'turbulent as the waters, you will no longer excel, for you went up onto your father’s bed, onto my couch and defiled it.'
Because he moved to Egypt early
49.correctAnswer: Because he was 'turbulent as the waters, you will no longer excel, for you went up onto your father’s bed, onto my couch and defiled it.'
49.explanation: 'Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, the first sign of my strength... Turbulent as the waters, you will no longer excel, for you went up onto your father’s bed, onto my couch and defiled it.'

49.question: What prophetic judgment was pronounced on Simeon and Levi because of their violent wrath at Shechem?
options: 'Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel! I will scatter them in Jacob and disperse them in Israel.'
They would be given all the chariots
49.correctAnswer: 'Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel! I will scatter them in Jacob and disperse them in Israel.'
49.explanation: 'Simeon and Levi are brothers—their swords are weapons of violence... Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel! I will scatter them in Jacob and disperse them in Israel.' (Levi was scattered among priestly cities; Simeon absorbed into Judah).

49.question: What majestic animal symbol did Jacob use to depict Judah in Genesis 49:9?
options: A lion's cub ('You are a lion’s cub, Judah; you return from the prey, my son. Like a lion he crouches and lies down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?')
49.correctAnswer: A lion's cub ('You are a lion’s cub, Judah; you return from the prey, my son. Like a lion he crouches and lies down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?')
49.explanation: 'You are a lion’s cub, Judah; you return from the prey, my son. Like a lion he crouches and lies down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?' (The Lion of the Tribe of Judah).

49.question: What famous messianic prophecy regarding kingship is recorded for Judah in Genesis 49:10?
options: 'The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come (until Shiloh comes) and the obedience of the nations shall be his.'
'Judah will be scattered in the desert'
49.correctAnswer: 'The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come (until Shiloh comes) and the obedience of the nations shall be his.'
49.explanation: Genesis 49:10 is the great messianic promise: 'The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come and the obedience of the nations shall be his.'

49.question: How did Jacob characterize Zebulun and Issachar in Genesis 49:13–15?
options: Zebulun as priests; Issachar as kings
Zebulun will live by the seashore and become a haven for ships; Issachar is a rawboned donkey lying down between two saddlebags
49.correctAnswer: Zebulun will live by the seashore and become a haven for ships; Issachar is a rawboned donkey lying down between two saddlebags
49.explanation: 'Zebulun will live by the seashore and become a haven for ships... Issachar is a rawboned donkey lying down between two saddlebags.'

49.question: What creature is Dan compared to in Genesis 49:16–17?
options: A snake by the roadside, a viper along the path, that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward
49.correctAnswer: A snake by the roadside, a viper along the path, that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward
49.explanation: 'Dan will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Dan will be a snake by the roadside, a viper along the path, that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.'

49.question: What spontaneous prayer of hope did Jacob interject in Genesis 49:18?
options: 'I look for your deliverance, Lord (I have waited for your salvation, O Lord)!'
49.correctAnswer: 'I look for your deliverance, Lord (I have waited for your salvation, O Lord)!'
49.explanation: Genesis 49:18 records Jacob's heartfelt prayer: 'I look for your deliverance, Lord!'

49.question: How did Jacob describe Joseph in Genesis 49:22–26?
options: A fruitful vine near a spring, whose branches climb over a wall... archers attacked him with bitterness, yet his bow remained steady, his strong arms stayed supple, because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob
A lonely shepherd in the hills
49.correctAnswer: A fruitful vine near a spring, whose branches climb over a wall... archers attacked him with bitterness, yet his bow remained steady, his strong arms stayed supple, because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob
49.explanation: Joseph is praised as a fruitful bough whose branches run over the wall, blessed with blessings of the heavens above and the deep beneath by the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel.

49.question: What final instructions did Jacob give all his sons before drawing his feet into the bed and breathing his last?
options: To build him a pyramid in Egypt
To bury him with his fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite (Machpelah), where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah were buried
To scatter his ashes on the Nile
49.correctAnswer: To bury him with his fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite (Machpelah), where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah were buried
49.explanation: Jacob commanded them: 'Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite... There Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah were buried, and there I buried Leah.' When Jacob finished giving instructions, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last and was gathered to his people.

50.question: How many days did the physicians take to embalm Jacob, and for how many days did the Egyptians mourn for him?
options: 40 days required for embalming; and the Egyptians mourned for him 70 days
50.correctAnswer: 40 days required for embalming; and the Egyptians mourned for him 70 days
50.explanation: Genesis 50:2–3 states that taking the full forty days for embalming was customary, and the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days (a royal Egyptian state mourning period).

50.question: What permission did Joseph request from Pharaoh through his court officials in Genesis 50:4–6?
options: To go up and bury his father in the tomb Jacob had dug for himself in the land of Canaan, in accordance with the solemn oath he had sworn
To build a palace at Beersheba
50.correctAnswer: To go up and bury his father in the tomb Jacob had dug for himself in the land of Canaan, in accordance with the solemn oath he had sworn
50.explanation: Joseph asked Pharaoh: 'My father made me swear an oath and said, I am about to die; bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan. Now let me go up and bury my father; then I will return.' Pharaoh answered: 'Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.'

50.question: Who accompanied Joseph and his brothers on the great funeral cortege to Canaan?
options: All Pharaoh's officials, the dignitaries of his court, all the dignitaries of Egypt, the households of Joseph and his brothers, along with chariots and horsemen—a very large company
50.correctAnswer: All Pharaoh's officials, the dignitaries of his court, all the dignitaries of Egypt, the households of Joseph and his brothers, along with chariots and horsemen—a very large company
50.explanation: A very large company went up: all Pharaoh's court officials, Egyptian elders, the entire family of Israel, and armed chariots and horsemen.

50.question: Where did they hold a seven-day period of deep, loud mourning, prompting the Canaanites to name the site Abel Mizraim ('mourning of the Egyptians')?
options: At the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan
50.correctAnswer: At the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan
50.explanation: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan, they lamented loudly and bitterly; and there Joseph observed a seven-day period of mourning for his father. The Canaanites called it Abel Mizraim.

50.question: Where was Jacob buried in fulfillment of his oath?
options: In the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought as a burial site from Ephron the Hittite
50.correctAnswer: In the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought as a burial site from Ephron the Hittite
50.explanation: His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought along with the field as a burial site from Ephron the Hittite.

50.question: What fear seized Joseph's brothers after their father Jacob had died in Genesis 50:15?
options: 'What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?'
That the Canaanites would invade Goshen
That they had lost all their grain
50.correctAnswer: 'What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?'
50.explanation: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, 'What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?'

50.question: What message and plea did the brothers send to Joseph in Genesis 50:16–18?
options: They sent word saying their father had commanded before he died: 'Forgive your brothers the sins and wrongs they committed in treating you so badly.' Then they threw themselves down before him: 'We are your slaves.'
They threatened to return to Canaan
50.correctAnswer: They sent word saying their father had commanded before he died: 'Forgive your brothers the sins and wrongs they committed in treating you so badly.' Then they threw themselves down before him: 'We are your slaves.'
50.explanation: They pleaded for forgiveness in the name of the God of their father, throwing themselves down before him saying, 'We are your slaves.'

50.question: What famous theological declaration of divine providence and forgiveness did Joseph speak to his weeping brothers in Genesis 50:19–21?
options: 'I will punish you for ten years'

'Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God? You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives. So then, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your children.'
'You must give me all your silver'
'I will never forgive what you did'
50.correctAnswer: 'Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God? You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives. So then, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your children.'
50.explanation: Genesis 50:20 is the grand theological climax of Genesis: 'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives. So then, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your children.' And he reassured them and spoke kindly to them.

50.question: How old was Joseph when he died, and what family milestone did he live to see?
options: 110 years old; he lived to see the third generation of Ephraim’s children, and the children of Makir son of Manasseh were placed at birth on Joseph’s knees
147 years old; he saw the Exodus
50.correctAnswer: 110 years old; he lived to see the third generation of Ephraim’s children, and the children of Makir son of Manasseh were placed at birth on Joseph’s knees
50.explanation: Joseph stayed in Egypt, along with all his father’s family. He lived a hundred and ten years and saw the third generation of Ephraim’s children. Also the children of Makir son of Manasseh were placed at birth on Joseph’s knees.

50.question: What oath of faith did Joseph make the Israelites swear before his death regarding his bones?
options: To build him a shrine in Memphis
'God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.' When he died at 110, he was embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.
To bury him in the Red Sea
To scatter his bones in the desert
50.correctAnswer: 'God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.' When he died at 110, he was embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.
50.explanation: Joseph said: 'I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and take you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.' And Joseph made the Israelites swear an oath: 'God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.'
